patterns.name: Hash the complement
patterns.idea: One pass: look up what you still need, then store what you have.
patterns.invariant: Every element before i is in the map, so the partner of nums[i] is a lookup.
patterns.cue: Find a pair/triple with a target sum or difference in unsorted data.

problems.title: Two Sum IV - Input is a BST
Pairs of Songs With Total Durations Divisible by 60
Count Nice Pairs in an Array

steps: One pass: *look up* what you need, then *store* what you have
nums[0] = 5: need *5*, is it in the map?
Not yet: store 5 → 0
nums[1] = 2: need *8*, is it in the map?
Not yet: store 2 → 1
nums[2] = 11: need *-1*, is it in the map?
Not yet: store 11 → 2
nums[3] = 7: need *3*, is it in the map?
Not yet: store 7 → 3
nums[4] = 3: need *7*, is it in the map?
Yes: 7 was stored at index 3. Answer *[3, 4]*
Every earlier element is in the map, so each check is *O(1)*: total *O(n)*

patterns.name: Frequency counting
patterns.idea: Count first; the answer is a question about the counts.
patterns.invariant: The counter is exact for everything seen so far.
patterns.cue: Anagrams, majority, 'first unique', top-k, 'can be formed from'.
patterns.complexity: O(n) time, O(k) space for k distinct keys

problems.title: First Unique Character in a String
Find All Duplicates in an Array

steps: Equal letter counts ⇔ equal *sorted key*; bucket by the key
'eat' sorts to *'aet'*: new bucket
'tea' sorts to *'aet'*: join its bucket
'tan' sorts to *'ant'*: new bucket
'ate' sorts to *'aet'*: join its bucket
'nat' sorts to *'ant'*: join its bucket
'bat' sorts to *'abt'*: new bucket
Three buckets: [eat tea ate] [tan nat] [bat]
Sorting each word costs k log k: *O(n · k log k)*; counting letters makes it O(n·k)

patterns.name: Canonical key hashing
patterns.idea: Map each item to a canonical form; equal forms share a bucket.
patterns.invariant: Two items are 'the same' iff their keys are equal.
patterns.cue: Grouping by structure: anagrams, shifted strings, isomorphism, duplicate subtrees.
patterns.example: Group Shifted Strings: 'abc','bcd','xyz' share the key (1,1)
steps: Shifting every letter keeps the *gaps* between letters: hash the gaps
'abc' → gaps *(1,1)*: new group
'bcd' → gaps *(1,1)*: same group as abc
'ace' → gaps *(2,2)*: new group
'xyz' → gaps *(1,1)*: same group as abc
'az' → gaps *(25)*: new group
'ba' → gaps *(25)*: same group as az
'a' → gaps *(·)*: new group
'z' → gaps *(·)*: same group as a
Equal keys ⇔ same shifted family: four groups
Build each key in O(k): *O(n · k)* total

patterns.name: In-place index hashing
patterns.idea: Values 1..n: mark presence by negating or swapping into slot value-1.
patterns.invariant: After pass one, index v-1 is marked iff value v was seen.
patterns.cue: Find missing/duplicate numbers in 1..n with O(1) extra space.

problems.title: Find All Numbers Disappeared in an Array
Find All Duplicates in an Array

patterns.example: First Missing Positive on [3,4,-1,1] via cyclic swaps
steps: The array itself is the hash: slot *v−1* should hold *v*
nums[0] = 3 belongs at index 2: *swap* it home
nums[0] = -1: out of range, *move on*
nums[1] = 4 belongs at index 3: *swap* it home
nums[1] = 1 belongs at index 0: *swap* it home
nums[1] = -1: out of range, *move on*
nums[2] = 3: already home, *move on*
nums[3] = 4: already home, *move on*
Scan: index 0 holds 1 ✓
Scan: index 1 holds -1, not 2. Missing = *2*
Each swap parks one value for good: *O(n)* time, *O(1)* extra space

patterns.name: Set-start expansion
patterns.idea: Only start a run from numbers whose predecessor is absent.
patterns.invariant: Each number is visited at most twice across all runs.
patterns.cue: Longest consecutive sequence in unsorted data.
steps: Put everything in a set; only *start* a run where x−1 is absent
100 starts a run: count up while present → length *1*
4: 3 is in the set, so 4 is *not a run start*, skip
200 starts a run: count up while present → length *1*
1 starts a run: count up while present → length *4*
3: 2 is in the set, so 3 is *not a run start*, skip
2: 1 is in the set, so 2 is *not a run start*, skip
Longest run: 1,2,3,4 → *4*
Each number is checked at most twice: *O(n)* with a set

patterns.name: Seen-set cycle detection
patterns.idea: Repeating a deterministic step: a repeated state means a cycle.
patterns.invariant: Every state visited so far is in the set.
patterns.cue: Happy numbers, digit games, linked structures when extra memory is fine.
steps: Repeat a deterministic step; a *repeated* value means a cycle, 1 means happy
19 is new: add it to seen, then 1² + 9² = *82*
Move to 82, check the set
82 is new: add it to seen, then 8² + 2² = *68*
Move to 68, check the set
68 is new: add it to seen, then 6² + 8² = *100*
Move to 100, check the set
100 is new: add it to seen, then 1² + 0² + 0² = *1*
Move to 1, check the set
Reached *1*: the number is happy
The set stops any loop; values stay small, so *O(log n)*-ish steps

patterns.name: Prefix sum + hashmap
patterns.idea: Subarray sum = prefix[j] − prefix[i]; count earlier prefixes worth prefix[j] − k.
patterns.invariant: The map holds the count of every prefix sum seen before j.
patterns.cue: Count/find subarrays with a given sum, divisible sum, or balanced 0/1.

problems.title: Maximum Size Subarray Sum Equals k

patterns.example: Subarray Sum Equals K on [1,2,3,-2,2], k=3
steps: sum(i..j) = prefix[j] − prefix[i]: count earlier prefixes equal to *prefix[j] − k*
Seed the map with prefix 0 seen once
prefix = 1; need 1 − 3 = *-2*, seen 0 times
Record prefix 1 in the map
prefix = 3; need 3 − 3 = *0*, seen 1 time
Each such prefix is one subarray ending here: count = *1*
Record prefix 3 in the map
prefix = 6; need 6 − 3 = *3*, seen 1 time
Each such prefix is one subarray ending here: count = *2*
Record prefix 6 in the map
prefix = 4; need 4 − 3 = *1*, seen 1 time
Each such prefix is one subarray ending here: count = *3*
Record prefix 4 in the map
prefix = 6; need 6 − 3 = *3*, seen 1 time
Each such prefix is one subarray ending here: count = *4*
Record prefix 6 in the map
Subarrays summing to 3: [1,2], [3], [3,−2,2] → *3*
One pass with a hash map: *O(n)* time, *O(n)* space

patterns.name: Prefix and suffix products
patterns.idea: Answer at i = everything to the left × everything to the right.
patterns.invariant: left[i] is the product of nums[0..i-1]; right[i] of nums[i+1..].
patterns.cue: 'Product except self', pivot index, best split point, two-sided aggregates.
patterns.complexity: O(n) time, O(1) extra with the output array

problems.title: Find the Middle Index in Array

patterns.example: Product of Array Except Self on [1,2,3,4]
steps: No division: answer[i] = (product on the *left*) × (product on the *right*)
left[0] = *1*: nothing is before index 0
left[1] = 1 (product of nums[0..0])
left[2] = 2 (product of nums[0..1])
left[3] = 6 (product of nums[0..2])
right[3] = *1*: nothing is after index 3
right[2] = 4 (product of nums[3..3])
right[1] = 12 (product of nums[2..3])
right[0] = 24 (product of nums[1..3])
Multiply column-wise: *[24, 12, 8, 6]*
Two passes, and right can be a running scalar: *O(n)* time, O(1) extra

patterns.name: Difference array (range add)
patterns.idea: Add at l, subtract at r+1; a prefix sum replays every range update.
patterns.invariant: prefix(diff)[i] equals the total added to position i.
patterns.cue: Many range increments, then read all values; car pooling, bookings.

problems.title: Number of Flowers in Full Bloom
Minimum Number of K Consecutive Bit Flips

steps: A range add becomes *two* point edits: +k at l, −k at r
Trip of 2 boards at stop 1: diff[1] += 2
…and leaves at stop 5: diff[5] −= 2
Trip of 3 boards at stop 3: diff[3] += 3
…and leaves at stop 7: diff[7] −= 3
Stop 0: load = 0 + (0) = *0*
Stop 1: load = 0 + (2) = *2*
Stop 2: load = 2 + (0) = *2*
Stop 3: load = 2 + (3) = *5* > capacity!
Load peaks at 5 > 4 at stop 3: *false*
q updates + one prefix pass: *O(n + q)*

patterns.name: 2D prefix sums
patterns.idea: Rectangle sum from four corner lookups by inclusion–exclusion.
patterns.invariant: P[i][j] is the sum of the rectangle from (0,0) to (i-1,j-1).
patterns.cue: Many rectangle-sum queries, square with sum ≤ threshold, matrix block sums.

problems.title: Count Square Submatrices with All Ones
Maximum Side Length of a Square with Sum Less than or Equal to Threshold
Number of Submatrices That Sum to Target

patterns.example: Range Sum Query 2D on a 3×3 matrix
steps: Precompute *corner sums* once, then any rectangle is four lookups
Table complete: each cell = cell + above + left − diagonal
Query: sum of rows 1..2, cols 1..2 (the 6,3,2,0 block)
Build *O(m·n)*, then every query is *O(1)*

patterns.name: Opposite ends converge
patterns.idea: Sorted: too small → move left up, too big → move right down.
patterns.invariant: The answer, if it exists, lies within [l, r].
patterns.cue: Pair sums in sorted arrays, container with most water, palindromes.

problems.title: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted

steps: Sorted input: start at *both ends* and squeeze inward
l on the smallest, r on the largest
1 + 18 = 19 > 18: too big, move *r* left
1 + 15 = 16 < 18: too small, move *l* right
2 + 15 = 17 < 18: too small, move *l* right
4 + 15 = 19 > 18: too big, move *r* left
4 + 11 = 15 < 18: too small, move *l* right
7 + 11 = 18 = target: *found* [4, 5]
Each step discards one end for good: *O(n)* time, *O(1)* space

patterns.name: Fix one, two-pointer the rest
patterns.idea: Sort, pin index i, solve a 2-sum on the suffix; skip duplicates.
patterns.invariant: All triples with a smaller first index are already enumerated.
patterns.cue: k-sum problems, count triangles, closest triple.
steps: Sort, *pin* index i, then two-pointer the suffix for −nums[i]
Pin -4: need two numbers summing to *4*
-4 + -1 + 2 = -3 < 0: move *l* right
-4 + -1 + 2 = -3 < 0: move *l* right
-4 + 0 + 2 = -2 < 0: move *l* right
-4 + 1 + 2 = -1 < 0: move *l* right
Pin -1: need two numbers summing to *1*
Triples: [−1,−1,2] and [−1,0,1]; later pins are ≥ 0, no more sums to 0
n pins × linear two-pointer sweep: *O(n²)*

patterns.name: Reader / writer pointers
patterns.idea: The writer trails the reader and keeps only what qualifies.
patterns.invariant: nums[0..w) is the compacted answer so far.
patterns.cue: Remove duplicates/elements in place, move zeroes, string compression.

problems.title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array II

steps: *r* reads every element; *w* is where the next non-zero belongs
nums[0] = 0: nothing to keep, only *r* moves
nums[1] = 1 is non-zero: swap into slot 0, w → 1
nums[2] = 0: nothing to keep, only *r* moves
nums[3] = 3 is non-zero: swap into slot 1, w → 2
nums[4] = 12 is non-zero: swap into slot 2, w → 3
Prefix [0, w) holds every non-zero in order; zeros fell to the end
One reader, one writer, no extra array: *O(n)* time, *O(1)* space

patterns.name: Dutch national flag partition
patterns.idea: Three regions: lows, unknown, highs; one pass with low/mid/high pointers.
patterns.invariant: nums[..lo) are 0s, nums[hi+1..] are 2s, nums[lo..mid) are 1s.
patterns.cue: Sort three categories in place, partition around a pivot.

problems.title: Partition Array According to Given Pivot

steps: Three regions: *0s* before lo, *2s* after hi, unknown between mid and hi
lo and mid start at 0, hi at the last index
nums[mid] = 2: swap with hi, hi *shrinks*; mid stays (unknown came in)
nums[mid] = 0: swap with lo, both *advance*
nums[mid] = 0: swap with lo, both *advance*
nums[mid] = 2: swap with hi, hi *shrinks*; mid stays (unknown came in)
nums[mid] = 1: already in the middle region, mid *advances*
nums[mid] = 1: already in the middle region, mid *advances*
mid passed hi: no unknowns left, *[0,0,1,1,2,2]*
One pass, three pointers: *O(n)* time, *O(1)* space

patterns.name: Merge two sorted sequences
patterns.idea: Compare heads, take the smaller, advance that side.
patterns.invariant: Output is sorted and contains everything consumed so far.
patterns.cue: Merge arrays/lists, intersections, merge from the back when space is in place.
patterns.example: Merge Sorted Array [1,2,3] + [2,5,6] from the back
steps: Fill from the *back* so nothing unread is overwritten
i and j sit on the last real values, *k* on the last empty slot
6 ≥ 3: write nums2[2] = 6 at slot 5
5 ≥ 3: write nums2[1] = 5 at slot 4
3 > 2: write nums1[2] = 3 at slot 3
2 ≥ 2: write nums2[0] = 2 at slot 2
nums2 is used up; whatever is left in nums1 is already in place
Every element is written once: *O(n + m)*, in place

patterns.name: Two-sided max walls
patterns.idea: Water at i is bounded by the smaller side's running max; advance the smaller side.
patterns.invariant: The side being moved has the lower max, so its water is already decided.
patterns.cue: Trapping rain water, container variants, two-sided bounds.
steps: Water at i = min(max to the left, max to the right) − h[i]
Two pointers from the ends; each side remembers its *max wall* so far
h[l]=0 < h[r]=1: left side is the bound. water += 0 − 0 = *0*
h[r]=1 ≤ h[l]=1: right side is the bound. water += 1 − 1 = *0*
h[l]=1 < h[r]=2: left side is the bound. water += 1 − 1 = *0*
h[l]=0 < h[r]=2: left side is the bound. water += 1 − 0 = *1*
h[r]=2 ≤ h[l]=2: right side is the bound. water += 2 − 2 = *0*
h[r]=1 ≤ h[l]=2: right side is the bound. water += 2 − 1 = *1*
h[r]=2 ≤ h[l]=2: right side is the bound. water += 2 − 2 = *0*
h[l]=2 < h[r]=3: left side is the bound. water += 2 − 2 = *0*
h[l]=1 < h[r]=3: left side is the bound. water += 2 − 1 = *1*
h[l]=0 < h[r]=3: left side is the bound. water += 2 − 0 = *2*
h[l]=1 < h[r]=3: left side is the bound. water += 2 − 1 = *1*
Pointers meet: total water *6*
The smaller side's max is already final, so one pass suffices: *O(n)*, *O(1)* space

patterns.name: Fixed-size window
patterns.idea: Slide a width-k window: add the new right, drop the old left.
patterns.invariant: The running aggregate describes exactly nums[r-k+1..r].
patterns.cue: Max average, anagram detection, k-length statistics.

problems.title: Find All Anagrams in a String
Maximum Number of Vowels in a Substring of Given Length
Number of Sub-arrays of Size K and Average Greater than or Equal to Threshold

steps: Keep a running sum of exactly *k* elements: add the new right, drop the old left
The window is a *bracket* of k cells; its sum lives in the state panel
First window [0..3]: sum = 2
Slide: + 50 − 1 → sum = *51*
51 beats the best so far: best = *51*
Slide: + 3 − 12 → sum = *42*
Best window [1..4] averages *12.75*
Each element enters once and leaves once: *O(n)*

patterns.name: Longest valid window
patterns.idea: Grow right; while invalid, shrink left; record the longest valid span.
patterns.invariant: After the shrink loop, [l, r] is valid and l is as small as possible.
patterns.cue: Longest substring with ≤k distinct / no repeats / ≤k replacements.

problems.title: Frequency of the Most Frequent Element
Longest Substring with At Most Two Distinct Characters
Longest Substring with At Most K Distinct Characters

patterns.example: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters on 'abcabcbb'
steps: Grow *r*; while the window has a repeat, shrink *l*; record the longest valid span
Window [0..0] = 'a' is valid, length 1, best = *1*
Window [0..1] = 'ab' is valid, length 2, best = *2*
Window [0..2] = 'abc' is valid, length 3, best = *3*
'a' repeats at index 0: jump l to *1*
Window [1..3] = 'bca' is valid, length 3, best = *3*
'b' repeats at index 1: jump l to *2*
Window [2..4] = 'cab' is valid, length 3, best = *3*
'c' repeats at index 2: jump l to *3*
Window [3..5] = 'abc' is valid, length 3, best = *3*
'b' repeats at index 4: jump l to *5*
Window [5..6] = 'cb' is valid, length 2
'b' repeats at index 6: jump l to *7*
Window [7..7] = 'b' is valid, length 1
Longest: 'abc' → *3*
l and r only move right: *O(n)* with a last-seen map

patterns.name: Shortest satisfying window
patterns.idea: Grow right until the window satisfies; shrink left while it still does.
patterns.invariant: When recorded, [l, r] satisfies and no smaller l does.
patterns.cue: Minimum window substring, minimum size subarray sum.

problems.title: Shortest Subarray with Sum at Least K
Smallest Range Covering Elements from K Lists

steps: Grow *r* until the sum reaches the target, then shrink *l* while it still does
Add nums[0] = 2: sum = 2 < 7, keep growing
Add nums[1] = 3: sum = 5 < 7, keep growing
Add nums[2] = 1: sum = 6 < 7, keep growing
Add nums[3] = 2: sum = 8 ≥ 7, now shrink
[0..3] sums to 8 ≥ 7 with length 4: best = *4*; drop nums[0]
Add nums[4] = 4: sum = 10 ≥ 7, now shrink
[1..4] sums to 10 ≥ 7 with length 4: best = *4*; drop nums[1]
[2..4] sums to 7 ≥ 7 with length 3: best = *3*; drop nums[2]
Add nums[5] = 3: sum = 9 ≥ 7, now shrink
[3..5] sums to 9 ≥ 7 with length 3: best = *3*; drop nums[3]
[4..5] sums to 7 ≥ 7 with length 2: best = *2*; drop nums[4]
Shortest window: [4..5] = [4, 3] → *2*
Both pointers move right only: *O(n)*

patterns.name: Count windows via at-most(k) trick
patterns.idea: exactly(k) = atMost(k) − atMost(k−1); each window end adds r−l+1 subarrays.
patterns.invariant: For fixed r, every l' ≥ l gives a valid subarray, counted as r−l+1.
patterns.cue: Count subarrays with exactly k distinct / k odd numbers / sum constraints.

problems.title: Number of Substrings Containing All Three Characters
Count Subarrays With Score Less Than K
Count Complete Subarrays in an Array

steps: exactly(k) = *atMost(k) − atMost(k−1)*; each r adds r−l+1 windows
atMost(2): r=0, l=0 → +1 windows, total *1*
atMost(2): r=1, l=0 → +2 windows, total *3*
atMost(2): r=2, l=0 → +3 windows, total *6*
atMost(2): r=3, l=0 → +4 windows, total *10*
atMost(2): r=4, shrink to l=3 → +2 windows, total *12*
atMost(2) = *12*: every window with at most two distinct values
atMost(1): r=0, l=0 → +1 windows, total *1*
atMost(1): r=1, shrink to l=1 → +1 windows, total *2*
atMost(1): r=2, shrink to l=2 → +1 windows, total *3*
atMost(1): r=3, shrink to l=3 → +1 windows, total *4*
atMost(1): r=4, shrink to l=4 → +1 windows, total *5*
Two linear sweeps: *O(n)*

patterns.name: Window with a need-counter
patterns.idea: Track how many required characters are still missing; zero means satisfied.
patterns.invariant: missing == number of chars whose window count is below the requirement.
patterns.cue: Anagram windows, minimum window substring, character budgets.

problems.title: Substring with Concatenation of All Words
Find All Anagrams in a String

steps: A *need* counter per letter; *missing* = letters still short. Zero missing = match
'e' not needed
'i' not needed
'd' not needed; drop 'e'
'b' needed: need[b] → 0, missing → 1; drop 'i'
'a' needed: need[a] → 0, missing → 0; drop 'd' → *missing = 0*
Window [3..4] = 'ba' is a permutation of 'ab': *true*
Counter updates are O(1) per step: *O(n + alphabet)*

patterns.name: Matching with a stack
patterns.idea: Push openers; a closer must match the top, then pop.
patterns.invariant: The stack holds exactly the currently unclosed openers, innermost on top.
patterns.cue: Brackets, tag validation, path simplification, backspace strings.

problems.title: Remove All Adjacent Duplicates In String
Minimum Add to Make Parentheses Valid
Minimum Remove to Make Valid Parentheses
Check if a Parentheses String Can Be Valid

steps: Push every *opener*; a closer must match the *top*, then pop it
'{' opens: push it
'[' opens: push it
'(' opens: push it
')' closes the top '(': *match*, pop
']' closes the top '[': *match*, pop
'}' closes the top '{': *match*, pop
'(' opens: push it
End of input but '(' is still open: *invalid*
Each character is pushed or popped once: *O(n)*

patterns.name: Nested structure via stack
patterns.idea: On '[' push the current context; on ']' pop and fold the inner result into it.
patterns.invariant: The stack is the chain of enclosing contexts, outermost at the bottom.
patterns.cue: Decode strings, nested lists, mini interpreters, exclusive time of functions.
steps: On '[' *push* the current context; on ']' *pop* and fold the inner result into it
digit 3: repeat count = *3*
'[': push ('', 3); start a fresh inner string
letter 'a': append to the current string → 'a'
digit 2: repeat count = *2*
'[': push ('a', 2); start a fresh inner string
letter 'c': append to the current string → 'c'
Stack empty: decoded *'accaccacc'*
Each bracket pushes and pops once; cost is the *output length*

patterns.name: Expression evaluation
patterns.idea: Numbers to an operand stack; operators apply by precedence (or use RPN).
patterns.invariant: The stack holds partial results that are still waiting on a lower-precedence operator.
patterns.cue: Calculators, RPN, infix with +−×÷ and parentheses.

problems.title: Evaluate the Bracket Pairs of a String

steps: Push numbers; *×* and *÷* apply immediately to the top, *+* and *−* push a signed value
read digit 3: num = 3
pending '+': push *3*, then remember '+'
read digit 2: num = 2
pending '+': push *2*, then remember '×'
read digit 2: num = 2
pending '×': 2 × 2 = *4* replaces the top, then remember '-'
read digit 1: num = 1
pending '-': push *-1*
Sum the stack: 3 + 4 + -1 = *6*
One pass, precedence handled by applying × ÷ eagerly: *O(n)*

patterns.name: Auxiliary-min stack
patterns.idea: Store (value, min-so-far) per push so the minimum pops away with its value.
patterns.invariant: Top of the min stack is the minimum of everything currently stacked.
patterns.cue: Design: min/max stack, stack with increment, undo histories.

problems.title: Design a Stack With Increment Operation

steps: Store the *minimum so far* beside each value, so pops never need a rescan
push 5: min so far = min(5, —) = *5*
push 2: min so far = min(2, 5) = *2*
push 7: min so far = min(7, 2) = *2*
push 1: min so far = min(1, 2) = *1*
getMin: read the top of the min stack → *1*
pop: remove 1 *and* its min entry together
getMin: read the top of the min stack → *2*
The min stack top is always the minimum of what remains: every op *O(1)*

patterns.name: Collision simulation
patterns.idea: Push moving things; when a newcomer collides with the top, resolve and maybe keep popping.
patterns.invariant: Everything on the stack can no longer collide with anything else on it.
patterns.cue: Asteroid collision, car fleets, robot crashes, meeting of opposite movers.

problems.title: Build an Array With Stack Operations

steps: Only a right-mover on the stack can hit a new *left-mover*
Next asteroid *5* (right)
No collision: push *5*
Next asteroid *10* (right)
No collision: push *10*
Next asteroid *-5* (left)
-5 hits 10: 10 is bigger, *-5 explodes*
Next asteroid *-11* (left)
-11 hits 10: 11 > 10, *10 explodes*, keep checking
-11 hits 5: 11 > 5, *5 explodes*, keep checking
No collision: push *-11*
Next asteroid *3* (right)
No collision: push *3*
Survivors: *[−11, 3]*
Each asteroid is pushed once and popped at most once: *O(n)*

patterns.name: Next greater element
patterns.idea: Keep a decreasing stack; a bigger newcomer resolves everything smaller on top.
patterns.invariant: The stack holds indices whose next-greater is not yet seen, values decreasing.
patterns.cue: Next greater/warmer day, stock span, 'how many until bigger'.

problems.title: Number of Visible People in a Queue
Final Prices With a Special Discount in a Shop

steps: A *decreasing* stack of indices still waiting for a warmer day
Push index 0 (73): it is now waiting for a warmer day
74 > 73: pop index 0, answer[0] = 1 − 0 = *1*
Then push index 1 (74)
75 > 74: pop index 1, answer[1] = 2 − 1 = *1*
Then push index 2 (75)
Push index 3 (71): it is now waiting for a warmer day
Push index 4 (69): it is now waiting for a warmer day
72 > 69: pop index 4, answer[4] = 5 − 4 = *1*
72 > 71: pop index 3, answer[3] = 5 − 3 = *2*
Then push index 5 (72)
76 > 72: pop index 5, answer[5] = 6 − 5 = *1*
76 > 75: pop index 2, answer[2] = 6 − 2 = *4*
Then push index 6 (76)
Push index 7 (73): it is now waiting for a warmer day
End: indices left on the stack never see a warmer day, answer stays *0*
Each index is pushed once and popped at most once: *O(n)*

patterns.name: Largest rectangle (bounds by pops)
patterns.idea: An increasing stack; popping a bar fixes its left and right smaller neighbours.
patterns.invariant: Bars on the stack are the left boundaries still open, heights increasing.
patterns.cue: Largest rectangle in histogram, maximal rectangle, sum of subarray minimums.

problems.title: Maximum Score of a Good Subarray

steps: An *increasing* stack: popping a bar fixes both of its smaller neighbours
Bar 0 (h=2) ≥ top: *push* index 0
Pop 0 (h=2): bounded by the start and 1, width 1, area *2*
Bar 1 (h=1) ≥ top: *push* index 1
Bar 2 (h=5) ≥ top: *push* index 2
Bar 3 (h=6) ≥ top: *push* index 3
Pop 3 (h=6): bounded by 2 and 4, width 1, area *6*
Pop 2 (h=5): bounded by 1 and 4, width 2, area *10*
Bar 4 (h=2) ≥ top: *push* index 4
Bar 5 (h=3) ≥ top: *push* index 5
Pop 5 (h=3): bounded by 4 and 6, width 1, area *3*
Pop 4 (h=2): bounded by 1 and 6, width 4, area *8*
Pop 1 (h=1): bounded by the start and 6, width 6, area *6*
Sentinel 0 flushed the stack
Largest rectangle: 5 × 2 = *10* (heights 5 and 6)
Each bar is pushed and popped once: *O(n)*

patterns.name: Greedy removal with a stack
patterns.idea: Pop a bigger previous digit while you still have removals left.
patterns.invariant: The kept prefix is the lexicographically smallest reachable so far.
patterns.cue: Remove k digits, smallest subsequence, competitive subsequence, remove duplicate letters.

problems.title: Minimum Deletions to Make String Balanced

steps: Pop a *bigger* previous digit while removals remain
Digit *1*
Keep 1

Keep 4
Digit *3*

Keep 3
Digit *2*
3 > 2: *remove 3*, k = 1
Keep 2

Keep 2
Digit *1*

Keep 1
Digit *9*
Keep 9

patterns.name: Previous and next smaller (both sides)
patterns.idea: One pass finds both neighbours: the popped element's right bound is the popper.
patterns.invariant: Each index gets its previous-smaller when pushed and next-smaller when popped.
patterns.cue: Contribution sums, maximum width ramp, 132 pattern, visible counts.

problems.title: Minimum Number of Increments on Subarrays to Form a Target Array
The Number of Weak Characters in the Game

steps: Pass 1: push only indices that are *smaller than every earlier* value
6 is a new minimum: push index *0*

nums[0]=6 ≤ nums[2]=8: ramp width *2*
Widest ramp: i=1 (0) to j=5 (5), width *4*
Two linear passes, each index pushed and popped once: *O(n)*

patterns.name: Monotonic deque window max
patterns.idea: A deque of candidates, decreasing; front is the window max; drop fronts that left the window.
patterns.invariant: Deque indices lie inside the window and their values are decreasing.
patterns.cue: Sliding window max/min, shortest subarray with sum ≥ k, jump game with deque DP.

problems.title: Longest Continuous Subarray With Absolute Diff Less Than or Equal to Limit
Shortest Subarray with Sum at Least K

steps: Front of the deque is the window max; the back holds *smaller, newer* candidates
Add *1*: push index 0 at the back
Add *3*: drop smaller tail 1, push 1
Add *-1*: push index 2 at the back
Window [0..2] max = front = *3*
Add *-3*: push index 3 at the back
Window [1..3] max = front = *3*
Add *5*: drop smaller tails -3, -1, 3, push 4
Window [2..4] max = front = *5*
Add *3*: push index 5 at the back
Window [3..5] max = front = *5*
Add *6*: drop smaller tails 3, 5, push 6
Window [4..6] max = front = *6*
Add *7*: drop smaller tail 6, push 7
Window [5..7] max = front = *7*
Each index enters and leaves the deque once: *O(n)*

patterns.name: Queue over a time window
patterns.idea: Push timestamps; pop from the front while they fall outside the window.
patterns.invariant: The queue holds exactly the events in the last W units.
patterns.cue: Hit counters, rate limiters, moving averages, recent requests.
steps: Keep every hit in a queue; drop fronts older than *t − 300*
hit(1): *append* 1
hit(2): *append* 2
hit(3): *append* 3
getHits(4) = queue length = *3*
hit(300): *append* 300
getHits(300) = queue length = *4*

getHits(301) = queue length = *3*
hit(302): *append* 302
getHits(303): 2, 3 ≤ 3, *pop* from the front
getHits(303) = queue length = *2*
Each timestamp enters and leaves once: *O(1)* amortised per call

patterns.name: Queue from two stacks
patterns.idea: Push to inbox; when outbox is empty, pour inbox over so the order flips.
patterns.invariant: outbox top is the oldest element not yet dequeued.
patterns.cue: Implement queue with stacks, undo/redo, amortised O(1) designs.
patterns.example: Queue via two stacks: push 1,2,3; pop; push 4; pop
steps: Two stacks: pushes land in *inbox*, pops come from *outbox*
push(1): onto inbox
push(2): onto inbox
push(3): onto inbox
pop(): outbox empty, *pour* inbox over, the order flips
pop() = *1*: the oldest element was on top of outbox
push(4): inbox again; outbox keeps the older ones
pop() = *2*: the oldest element was on top of outbox
pop() = *3*: the oldest element was on top of outbox
Outbox empty again: next pop pours *4* over
Each element is moved at most once: *O(1)* amortised per op

patterns.name: Classic binary search
patterns.idea: Halve the sorted range by comparing with the middle.
patterns.invariant: The target, if present, is inside [lo, hi].
patterns.cue: Sorted array lookups, first/last position, insert position, 2D matrix search.

problems.title: Find First and Last Position of Element in Sorted Array
Search in a Sorted Array of Unknown Size

steps: The target, if present, lives inside *[lo, hi]*
5 < 9: drop the left half, lo = *4*
12 > 9: drop the right half, hi = *4*
nums[4] = 9: *found* at index 4
Each step halves the range: *O(log n)* comparisons

patterns.name: First true (predicate boundary)
patterns.idea: A monotone false…true predicate: find the first index where it flips.
patterns.invariant: pred(lo−1) is false and pred(hi) is true (or hi is past the end).
patterns.cue: First bad version, lower/upper bound, leftmost insertion, 'minimum x such that'.

problems.title: Find First and Last Position of Element in Sorted Array
Peak Index in a Mountain Array
Find Smallest Letter Greater Than Target

patterns.example: First Bad Version with n=8, first bad = 5
steps: A monotone predicate: find the *first* index where it turns true
mid = 4: isBad(4) = *false*
Good: the first bad is *after* 4, lo = 5
mid = 6: isBad(6) = *true*
Bad: the first bad is 6 *or earlier*, hi = 6
mid = 5: isBad(5) = *true*
Bad: the first bad is 5 *or earlier*, hi = 5
lo == hi == 5: the *first bad version is 5*
Keep lo on 'maybe', hi on 'definitely true': *O(log n)* calls

patterns.name: Binary search on the answer
patterns.idea: Guess an answer, check feasibility greedily, tighten the range.
patterns.invariant: feasible(x) is monotone, so the smallest feasible x is a boundary.
patterns.cue: Split array largest sum, Koko bananas, ship capacity, minimize max / maximize min.

problems.title: Capacity To Ship Packages Within D Days

Find the Smallest Divisor Given a Threshold

Minimized Maximum of Products Distributed to Any Store

Feasible: try *slower*, hi = 6
Too slow: need *faster*, lo = 4
Feasible: try *slower*, hi = 5
Feasible: try *slower*, hi = 4
lo == hi: the minimum feasible speed is *4*
feasible(k) is monotone, so the answer is a boundary: *O(n log range)*

patterns.name: Rotated / mountain search
patterns.idea: One half is always sorted: decide which, then whether the target lives there.
patterns.invariant: At each step the target is inside the half you keep.
patterns.cue: Rotated sorted array search, minimum in rotated array, peak finding.

problems.title: Single Element in a Sorted Array

Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array

Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array II

steps: One half of [lo, hi] is always *sorted*; decide which, then where the target is
mid = 3, nums[mid] = *7*

0 is not in the sorted left half: go *right*, lo = 4
mid = 5, nums[mid] = *1*

mid = 4, nums[mid] = *0*

Still halving every step: *O(log n)*

patterns.name: Partition two sorted arrays
patterns.idea: Binary search the cut in the shorter array so left halves hold exactly half the items.
patterns.invariant: Every left element ≤ every right element once the cut is right.
patterns.cue: Median of two sorted arrays, kth element of two arrays.

steps: Binary search the cut in A so the *left halves hold half the items*
Try i = 2, j = 6 − 2 = 4: left maxes 3, 19 · right mins 8, 21

Try i = 4, j = 6 − 4 = 2: left maxes 9, 11 · right mins 15, 18
Every left ≤ every right: the cut is right, median = max(left) = *11*
Only the shorter array is searched: *O(log min(m, n))*

patterns.name: Sort and merge intervals
patterns.idea: Sort by start; extend the current interval when the next one overlaps.
patterns.invariant: The output is disjoint and sorted; the current interval may still grow.
patterns.cue: Merge, insert interval, employee free time, summary ranges.
steps: Sort by start; walk left to right keeping one *current* interval
[1,3] starts after the current end: *start a new* interval
[2,6] starts at 2 ≤ 6: overlaps, *extend* the end to 6
[8,10] starts after the current end: *start a new* interval
[15,18] starts after the current end: *start a new* interval
Done: [[1,6],[8,10],[15,18]], disjoint and sorted
Sort *O(n log n)*, then one linear sweep

patterns.name: Sweep line (events ±1)
patterns.idea: Turn intervals into +1/−1 events, sort, and sweep to track concurrency.

t = 30: end of [0,30], running = *0*

patterns.name: Earliest finish first
patterns.idea: Sort by end; take an interval whenever it starts after the last chosen end.
patterns.invariant: The chosen set is maximal among all compatible sets of the prefix.
patterns.cue: Non-overlapping intervals, arrows to burst balloons, activity selection.

patterns.name: Custom comparator / key sort
patterns.idea: Define 'better' pairwise or as a key, then sort once.
patterns.invariant: The comparator is a total order, so the sort is well-defined.

Concatenate: *9534330*
One sort with a pairwise rule: *O(n log n)* comparisons

patterns.name: Cyclic sort (1..n placement)
patterns.idea: Swap each value into its home index until every slot holds its own number.
patterns.invariant: Each swap places at least one value permanently; at most n swaps total.
patterns.cue: Missing/duplicate numbers in 1..n, first missing positive.

nums[0] = 3 belongs at index *2*: swap
After the swap 3 sits at 2; keep working on index 0
nums[0] = 5 belongs at index *4*: swap
After the swap 5 sits at 4; keep working on index 0
nums[0] = 2 belongs at index *1*: swap
After the swap 2 sits at 1; keep working on index 0
nums[0] = 1 is already home: *advance*
nums[1] = 2 is already home: *advance*
nums[2] = 3 is already home: *advance*
nums[3] = 4 is already home: *advance*
nums[4] = 5 is already home: *advance*
Sorted in place: *[1,2,3,4,5]*
Each swap homes one value for good: *O(n)* time, *O(1)* space

patterns.name: Quickselect (kth element)
patterns.idea: Partition around a pivot; recurse only into the side holding k.
patterns.invariant: After partition, the pivot is in its final sorted position.
patterns.cue: Kth largest, top-k without a heap, median.

problems.title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
Kth Largest Element in a Stream

steps: Partition around a pivot; recurse only into the *side that holds index 4*
Range [0, 5], pivot = last = *4*
3 < 4: swap into slot 0, store = 1
2 < 4: swap into slot 1, store = 2
1 < 4: swap into slot 2, store = 3
5 ≥ 4: leave it on the right
6 ≥ 4: leave it on the right
Place the pivot at index *3*: everything left is smaller
3 < 4: the answer is on the *right*
Range [4, 5], pivot = last = *5*
6 ≥ 5: leave it on the right
Place the pivot at index *4*: everything left is smaller
Index 4 is the target: the 2nd largest is *5*
One side per round, halving on average: *O(n)* expected

patterns.name: Merge sort with counting
patterns.idea: While merging, count cross pairs that violate the order.
patterns.invariant: Both halves are sorted, so each cross count is found with a pointer sweep.
patterns.cue: Count inversions, reverse pairs, count of smaller after self, range sums.

problems.title: Count of Smaller Numbers After Self

steps: Sort each half recursively; *count cross pairs* while merging
left 1: no right value r with 1 > 2·r
left 2: no right value r with 2 > 2·r
left 3: 1 right value with 3 > 2·r → pairs += *1*
Within each half the pairs were counted in the recursive calls (*1* there: 3 > 2·1)
Merge: take *1* from the left
Merge: take *1* from the right
Merge: take *2* from the left
Merge: take *3* from the left
Merge: take *3* from the right
Total reverse pairs: *2* (3>2·1, 3>2·1 from each 3)
Counting rides on the merge: *O(n log n)*

patterns.name: Bucket / counting sort
patterns.idea: Bounded keys: count into buckets instead of comparing.
patterns.invariant: bucket[v] holds every item with key v.
patterns.cue: Top-k by frequency, H-index, maximum gap, sort colours.
steps: Citations above n = 5 count as 5: *bucket by count* instead of sorting
paper with 3 citations → bucket *3*
paper with 0 citations → bucket *0*
paper with 6 citations → bucket *5*
paper with 1 citations → bucket *1*
paper with 5 citations → bucket *5*
Scan buckets from the top, accumulating papers with ≥ k citations
k = 5: 2 papers have ≥ 5 citations, 2 < 5, keep going
k = 4: 2 papers have ≥ 4 citations, 2 < 4, keep going
k = 3: 3 papers have ≥ 3 citations, 3 ≥ 3 → *h = 3*
Buckets replace the sort: *O(n)* time

patterns.name: Fast and slow pointers
patterns.idea: Two speeds: a cycle makes them meet; otherwise slow lands on the middle.
patterns.invariant: fast is always 2× as far from head as slow (until it meets or ends).
patterns.cue: Cycle detection, cycle start, middle node, palindrome list, happy number.

problems.title: Remove Nth Node From End of List

steps: Tortoise moves 1, hare moves 2: in a cycle the hare *laps* the tortoise
Step 1: slow → 2, fast → 0
Step 2: slow → 0, fast → 2
Step 3: both land on *-4*, they met → a cycle exists
To find the cycle start: reset one pointer to head, walk both at speed 1
Both advance one: 2 and 2 — they meet at the *cycle start*
Cycle begins at node *2*
No extra memory, at most 2n steps: *O(n)* time, *O(1)* space

patterns.name: In-place reversal
patterns.idea: Walk with prev/cur/next, flipping each pointer.
patterns.invariant: prev heads a fully reversed prefix; cur heads the untouched suffix.
patterns.cue: Reverse a list, reverse between m and n, reverse in k-groups, swap pairs.

Save next = 1 before we break the link
Flip: node 1 now points to *null*
Advance: prev = 1, cur = 2
Save next = 2 before we break the link
Flip: node 2 now points to *1*
Advance: prev = 2, cur = 3
Save next = 3 before we break the link
Flip: node 3 now points to *2*
Advance: prev = 3, cur = 4
Save next = 4 before we break the link
Flip: node 4 now points to *3*
Advance: prev = 4, cur = 5
Save next = null before we break the link
Flip: node 5 now points to *4*
Advance: prev = 5, cur = null
cur is null: *prev* is the new head, every arrow points back
One pass, three pointers: *O(n)* time, *O(1)* space

patterns.idea: A sentinel before head removes every 'is it the first node?' special case.
patterns.invariant: dummy.next is always the true head of the result.
patterns.cue: Remove elements, delete duplicates, partition list, merge lists.

problems.title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
Remove Duplicates from Sorted List II

fast → node 1 (step 1 of 3)
fast → node 2 (step 2 of 3)
fast → node 3 (step 3 of 3)
Advance both: slow → 1, fast → 4
Advance both: slow → 2, fast → 5
fast is at the tail, so slow is *just before* the node to remove

One pass, no head special-case: *O(n)* time

patterns.idea: Walk both lists, add digits plus carry, emit one node per position.

Write digit 0, carry = *1*
Write digit 8, carry = *0*

One node per position: *O(max(n, m))*

patterns.name: Clone with a map or interleaving

Copy node 7; map[7] = 7'
Copy node 13; map[13] = 13'
Copy node 11; map[11] = 11'
Pass 2: for each node, set copy.next = map[old.next] and copy.random = *map[old.random]*
7': next = map[13], random = map[null] = *null*
13': next = map[11], random = map[7] = *7'*
11': next = map[null], random = map[11] = *11'*
The copy is complete and shares no nodes with the original
Two passes, one map: *O(n)* time and space

patterns.name: Hash map + doubly linked list (LRU)
patterns.idea: A map for O(1) lookup, a list for O(1) recency moves; evict from the tail.
patterns.invariant: List order is recency: head most recent, tail least recent.
patterns.cue: LRU/LFU caches, 'move to front', most recently used queues.
patterns.example: LRU capacity 2: put 1, put 2, get 1, put 3, get 2
steps: A map finds a node in O(1); the list keeps *recency order* in O(1)
put(1,1): insert at the *front*, map[1] = node
put(2,2): insert at the *front*, map[2] = node
get(1) = *1*: found via the map, move it to the front
put(3,3): full, *evict the tail* key 2
put(3,3): insert at the *front*, map[3] = node
get(2) = *−1*: not in the map
put(4,4): full, *evict the tail* key 1
put(4,4): insert at the *front*, map[4] = node
get(1) = *−1*: not in the map
get(3) = *3*: found via the map, move it to the front
Every op touches one node and one map entry: *O(1)*

patterns.name: Recursive DFS (post-order fold)
patterns.idea: Solve the children, then combine at the parent.
patterns.invariant: f(node) depends only on f(left) and f(right).
patterns.cue: Height, balanced, same/symmetric tree, invert, count nodes.
steps: Ask the root: how deep is the tree below you?
The root cannot answer yet: it asks its *left* child first
9 has no children: it returns *1*
Now the *right* child, 20, is asked
20 asks its left child 15: a leaf, returns *1*
Then its right child 7: also a leaf, returns *1*
20 combines: 1 + max(1, 1) = *2*
Root combines: 1 + max(1, 2) = *3*
Every node is visited once and answers once: *O(n)*, stack depth *O(h)*

patterns.name: Best path through each node
patterns.idea: Each node returns its best single-branch; the answer considers both branches joined at the node.

Node 2: left 0, right 0 → path through it = 0 + 0 + 2 edges = *2*
Node 2 returns 1 + max(0, 0) = *1* upward
Leaf 3 returns *0*
Root: left 1 + right 0 + 2 edges = *3* > 2, new best
Root returns 1 + max(1, 0) = 2 (unused); the *diameter is 3*
One post-order pass: *O(n)*

patterns.name: Level-order BFS
patterns.idea: Process one level at a time: the queue length at loop start is the level size.
patterns.invariant: The queue holds exactly one level when a level begins.
patterns.cue: Level order, zigzag, right side view, level averages, max width, connect next pointers.
