Relax 3→4: 1 + 1 = 2 < 7, update and push
Pop the closest: (2,4). Node 4 is now *settled* at 2
Pop (7,4): node 4 is already settled, *stale*, skip
All settled: the farthest node is 4 at distance *2*, so the delay is 2
A popped node is final: *O(E log V)* with a binary heap

patterns.name: Bellman–Ford with k rounds
patterns.idea: Relax every edge k+1 times from a copy of the previous round.
patterns.invariant: After round i, dist[v] is the cheapest path using ≤ i edges.
patterns.cue: Cheapest flights within k stops, negative edges, bounded-edge paths.

problems.title: Minimum Cost to Reach Destination in Time

patterns.example: Cheapest Flights with k=1 on 4 cities
steps: dist[0] = 0, others ∞. Each round allows *one more edge*
Round 1: relax every edge using a *copy* of last round's values
0→1: 0 + 100 = *100* improves dist[1]
1→2: ∞ + 100 does not beat ∞, skip
2→0: ∞ + 100 does not beat 0, skip
1→3: ∞ + 600 does not beat ∞, skip
2→3: ∞ + 200 does not beat ∞, skip
Round 2: relax every edge using a *copy* of last round's values
0→1: 0 + 100 does not beat 100, skip
2→0: ∞ + 100 does not beat 0, skip
2→3: ∞ + 200 does not beat 700, skip
After k+1 = 2 rounds, dist[3] = *700* via 0→1→3 (0→1→2→3 needs 2 stops)
k+1 rounds over all edges: *O(k · E)*

patterns.name: Minimum spanning tree
patterns.idea: Kruskal: sort edges, union-find to skip cycles. Prim: grow from one node with a heap.
patterns.invariant: The chosen edges never form a cycle and stay minimal by the cut property.
patterns.cue: Min cost to connect points, water distribution, critical edges.

problems.title: Min Cost to Connect All Points
Optimize Water Distribution in a Village
Find Critical and Pseudo-Critical Edges in Minimum Spanning Tree

steps: Sort all 6 edges by weight; the MST needs *n − 1 = 3* of them
B–D (3): joins two components, *take it*, cost 3
A–B (4): joins two components, *take it*, cost 7
A–D (7): both already connected, would form a *cycle*, skip
B–C (9): joins two components, *take it*, cost 16
3 edges chosen: every point connected, total cost *16*
Cut property: the lightest edge leaving a component is always safe
Sorting dominates: *O(E log E)*; Prim with a heap is the same bound

patterns.name: Bipartite colouring
patterns.idea: BFS/DFS painting neighbours the opposite colour; a clash means odd cycle.
patterns.invariant: Every discovered edge joins two different colours.
patterns.cue: Is graph bipartite, possible bipartition, two-group splits.

problems.title: Divide Nodes Into the Maximum Number of Groups

patterns.example: Is Graph Bipartite? on a 4-node square plus a chord
steps: Paint node 0 purple and BFS; every neighbour gets the *opposite* colour
Pop 0: check each neighbour of 0
1 is unpainted: give it the *opposite* colour of 0
3 is unpainted: give it the *opposite* colour of 0
2 is unpainted: give it the *opposite* colour of 0
Pop 1: check each neighbour of 1
Edge 1–0: colours already differ, fine
Edge 1–2: *same colour* on both ends, an odd cycle
Not bipartite: the triangle 0-1-2 cannot be 2-coloured
One BFS over the graph: *O(V + E)*

patterns.name: Eulerian path (Hierholzer)
patterns.idea: Walk greedily, back out when stuck, and record nodes post-order; reverse at the end.
patterns.invariant: A node is appended only when all its edges are used.
patterns.cue: Reconstruct itinerary, valid arrangement of pairs, cracking the safe.
steps: Sort each airport's tickets; walk greedily, *back out* when stuck
Start at JFK
JFK still has a ticket: fly to *ATL*
ATL still has a ticket: fly to *JFK*
JFK still has a ticket: fly to *SFO*
SFO still has a ticket: fly to *ATL*
ATL still has a ticket: fly to *SFO*
SFO has no tickets left: *stuck*, write it at the end
ATL has no tickets left: *stuck*, write it at the end
SFO has no tickets left: *stuck*, write it at the end
JFK has no tickets left: *stuck*, write it at the end
ATL has no tickets left: *stuck*, write it at the end
JFK has no tickets left: *stuck*, write it at the end
Reversed post-order is the itinerary: *JFK ATL JFK SFO ATL SFO*
Every ticket is used once; sorting costs *O(E log E)*

patterns.name: Bridges / articulation (low-link)
patterns.idea: DFS timestamps; an edge is a bridge if the child cannot reach back above it.
patterns.invariant: low[v] = smallest discovery time reachable from v's subtree via one back edge.
patterns.cue: Critical connections, articulation points, strongly connected components.

problems.title: Minimum Number of Days to Disconnect Island
Number of Operations to Make Network Connected

patterns.example: Critical Connections on a 4-node graph with one bridge
steps: DFS stamps each node with a discovery time; low = earliest time reachable
Visit 0: disc = low = *0*
Visit 1: disc = low = *1*
Visit 2: disc = low = *2*
2 sees visited 0: back edge, low[2] = *0*
Back at 1: low[2] = 0 ≤ disc[1], 2 can climb above, *not* a bridge
Visit 3: disc = low = *3*
Back at 1: low[3] = 3 > disc[1] = 1, edge 1–3 is a *bridge*
Back at 0: low[1] = 0 ≤ disc[0], 1 can climb above, *not* a bridge
0 sees visited 2: back edge, low[0] = *0*
Only 1–3 is critical: removing it disconnects node 3
One DFS with timestamps: *O(V + E)*

patterns.name: Clone / traverse with a visited map
patterns.idea: Map original→copy; create a node the first time you see it, reuse afterwards.
patterns.invariant: Every visited original has exactly one clone.
patterns.cue: Clone graph, copy random list, keys and rooms, find if path exists.

problems.title: Find if Path Exists in Graph
All Paths From Source to Target

steps: Map original → clone; a node is cloned *once*, on first sight
First time at 1: create clone *1'* and record it in the map
First time at 2: create clone *2'* and record it in the map
1 already in the map: *reuse* 1' instead of cloning again
First time at 3: create clone *3'* and record it in the map
2 already in the map: *reuse* 2' instead of cloning again
First time at 4: create clone *4'* and record it in the map
3 already in the map: *reuse* 3' instead of cloning again
1 already in the map: *reuse* 1' instead of cloning again
Wire 3' → 4'
Wire 2' → 3'
Wire 1' → 2'
4 already in the map: *reuse* 4' instead of cloning again
Clone finished: same shape, 4 new nodes, every edge mirrored
Each node and edge handled once: *O(V + E)*

patterns.name: Implicit graph (states as nodes)
patterns.idea: Define neighbours by a rule instead of an adjacency list; search as usual.
patterns.invariant: A state is generated on demand and visited at most once.
patterns.cue: Word ladder, open the lock, minimum genetic mutation, water jug, guess the word.
patterns.example: Open the Lock from 0000 to 0202 avoiding dead ends
steps: No adjacency list: a state's *4 neighbours* are made by turning one wheel ±1
Start at 00, 0 turns; visited = {00}
Pop *00* (0 turns): generate its four neighbours
Pop *90* (1 turns): generate its four neighbours
push 80, 91, 99; 00 seen
*99* found at distance 2: the first visit is the shortest path
Each state visited once, 4 moves each: *O(10^w · w)* for w wheels

patterns.name: Subsets (include / exclude)
patterns.idea: At each index choose to take it or not; the leaf is one subset.
patterns.invariant: The partial choice list describes a unique prefix decision path.
patterns.cue: Subsets, subsets with duplicates, bitmask enumeration.

problems.title: Find Minimum Time to Finish All Jobs

steps: At each index: *take it or skip it*; every leaf is one subset
Index 0: *take* 1, push it on the path
Index 1: *take* 2, push it on the path
Index 2: *take* 3, push it on the path
Index 3 is past the end: record *123*
Back at index 2: *skip* 3, pop it off
Index 3 is past the end: record *12*
Back at index 1: *skip* 2, pop it off
Index 2: *take* 3, push it on the path
Index 3 is past the end: record *13*
Back at index 2: *skip* 3, pop it off
Index 3 is past the end: record *1*
Back at index 0: *skip* 1, pop it off
Index 1: *take* 2, push it on the path
Index 2: *take* 3, push it on the path
Index 3 is past the end: record *23*
Back at index 2: *skip* 3, pop it off
Index 3 is past the end: record *2*
Back at index 1: *skip* 2, pop it off
Index 2: *take* 3, push it on the path
Index 3 is past the end: record *3*
Back at index 2: *skip* 3, pop it off
Index 3 is past the end: record *∅*
8 = 2³ subsets, each index decided twice down every branch
Exponential by nature: *O(2^n · n)*

patterns.name: Permutations with a used set
patterns.idea: Pick any unused element next; undo the pick when you return.
patterns.invariant: used[] marks exactly the elements in the current path.
patterns.cue: Permutations, permutations II, next permutation, permutation sequence.

problems.title: Letter Combinations of a Phone Number

steps: Pick any *unused* number next; undo the pick when you return
Choose 1: mark used, push on the path
Choose 2: mark used, push on the path
Choose 3: mark used, push on the path
Path full: record *123*
Choose 3: mark used, push on the path
Choose 2: mark used, push on the path
Path full: record *132*
Undo 1: unmark it, pop, try the next unused
Choose 2: mark used, push on the path
Choose 1: mark used, push on the path
Choose 3: mark used, push on the path
Path full: record *213*
Choose 3: mark used, push on the path
Choose 1: mark used, push on the path
Path full: record *231*
Undo 2: unmark it, pop, try the next unused
Choose 3: mark used, push on the path
Choose 1: mark used, push on the path
Choose 2: mark used, push on the path
Path full: record *312*
Choose 2: mark used, push on the path
Choose 1: mark used, push on the path
Path full: record *321*
Undo 3: unmark it, pop, try the next unused
All *3! = 6* orders produced, none repeated
n choices, then n−1, …: *O(n · n!)*

patterns.name: Combination sum with a start index
patterns.idea: Only choose from index start onward so each combination is made once.
patterns.invariant: Choices are non-decreasing in index, so no duplicates appear.
patterns.cue: Combination sum I/II/III, combinations, palindrome partitioning.
patterns.complexity: O(k · C) time for C combinations

problems.title: Partition to K Equal Sum Subsets

steps: Reuse allowed, but only choose from *start* onward so each set is made once
Take 2 (start = 0): remaining 7 − 2 = *5*
Take 2 (start = 0): remaining 5 − 2 = *3*
Take 2 (start = 0): remaining 3 − 2 = *1*
2 > remaining 1: candidates are sorted, *prune* the rest
Take 3 (start = 1): remaining 3 − 3 = *0*
remaining = 0: *2+2+3* is a valid combination
6 > remaining 3: candidates are sorted, *prune* the rest
Take 3 (start = 1): remaining 5 − 3 = *2*
3 > remaining 2: candidates are sorted, *prune* the rest
6 > remaining 5: candidates are sorted, *prune* the rest
Take 3 (start = 1): remaining 7 − 3 = *4*
Take 3 (start = 1): remaining 4 − 3 = *1*
3 > remaining 1: candidates are sorted, *prune* the rest
6 > remaining 4: candidates are sorted, *prune* the rest
Take 6 (start = 2): remaining 7 − 6 = *1*
6 > remaining 1: candidates are sorted, *prune* the rest
Take 7 (start = 3): remaining 7 − 7 = *0*
remaining = 0: *7* is a valid combination
Found *2+2+3* and *7*; 3+2+2 never appears because start only moves forward
Branching bounded by target / smallest candidate: exponential, but pruned

patterns.name: Grid DFS with undo
patterns.idea: Mark the cell, explore four ways, unmark on return.
patterns.invariant: Marked cells are exactly the current path.
patterns.cue: Word search, word search II (with trie), unique paths III, N-queens-style boards.
patterns.example: Word Search for 'SEE' in a 3×4 board
steps: Mark a cell, explore 4 neighbours, *unmark* on the way back
(1,0) = 'S' matches *'S'*: mark it, depth 1
(1,1) = 'F' ≠ 'E': dead end
(2,0) = 'A' ≠ 'E': dead end
(0,0) = 'A' ≠ 'E': dead end
No way on from (1,0): *unmark* it and back up
(1,3) = 'S' matches *'S'*: mark it, depth 1
(2,3) = 'E' matches *'E'*: mark it, depth 2
(2,2) = 'E' matches *'E'*: mark it, depth 3
Last letter matched: *found* 'SEE'
Each start cell tries 4^L paths at worst: *O(m·n·4^L)*

patterns.name: Constraint placement with pruning
patterns.idea: Place one item per row/cell; check constraints before recursing; prune early.
patterns.invariant: Every partial board satisfies all constraints so far.
patterns.cue: N-queens, sudoku solver, valid arrangement, 24 game.

problems.title: Partition to K Equal Sum Subsets

steps: Place one queen per row; a cell is legal only if no column or diagonal is taken
Row 0: column 0 is free, *place* a queen
Row 1: column 2 is free, *place* a queen
Row 2: every column attacked, *backtrack* to row 1
Row 1, column 2 leads nowhere: *remove* it, try the next column
Row 1: column 3 is free, *place* a queen
Row 2: column 1 is free, *place* a queen
Row 3: every column attacked, *backtrack* to row 2
Row 2, column 1 leads nowhere: *remove* it, try the next column
Row 2: every column attacked, *backtrack* to row 1
Row 1, column 3 leads nowhere: *remove* it, try the next column
Row 1: every column attacked, *backtrack* to row 0
Row 0, column 0 leads nowhere: *remove* it, try the next column
Row 0: column 1 is free, *place* a queen
Row 1: column 3 is free, *place* a queen
Row 2: column 0 is free, *place* a queen
Row 3: column 2 is free, *place* a queen
All 4 rows filled: *solution* found
Sets for columns and diagonals make each check *O(1)*; pruning kills most branches

patterns.name: Generate valid sequences
patterns.idea: Add '(' while opens remain; add ')' only while closes < opens.
patterns.invariant: Every prefix has at least as many '(' as ')'.
patterns.cue: Generate parentheses, remove invalid parentheses, letter combinations.

problems.title: Letter Combinations of a Phone Number

steps: Add '(' while opens < n; add ')' only while *closes < opens*
opens = 0 < 2: add *'('*
opens = 1 < 2: add *'('*
opens = 2: no more '(' allowed
closes = 0 < opens = 2: add *')'*
opens = 2: no more '(' allowed
closes = 1 < opens = 2: add *')'*
Length 4 reached: *(())* is valid by construction
closes = 0 < opens = 1: add *')'*
opens = 1 < 2: add *'('*
opens = 2: no more '(' allowed
closes = 1 < opens = 2: add *')'*
Length 4 reached: *()()* is valid by construction
closes = opens = 1: a ')' here would be *invalid*, prune
closes = opens = 0: a ')' here would be *invalid*, prune
Exactly *2* strings: (()) and ()(), the Catalan number C₂
Output count is Catalan(n); each string costs O(n)

patterns.name: 1-D linear DP
patterns.idea: dp[i] from dp[i−1] and dp[i−2]; roll two variables.
patterns.invariant: dp[i] is the answer for the prefix ending at i.
patterns.cue: Climbing stairs, house robber, min cost climbing, decode ways, fibonacci.
steps: dp[i] = max(dp[i−1], dp[i−2] + nums[i]): *skip* house i or *rob* it
dp[0] = 2: only one house, rob it
Answer is dp[4] = *12*: rob houses 0, 2 and 4
Only dp[i−1] and dp[i−2] are needed: *O(n)* time, *O(1)* space

patterns.name: Kadane (best ending here)
patterns.idea: best ending at i = max(nums[i], best ending at i−1 + nums[i]).
patterns.invariant: cur is the maximum subarray sum that ends exactly at i.
patterns.cue: Maximum subarray, max product subarray, max circular subarray, stock I.

problems.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
Maximum Absolute Sum of Any Subarray

steps: cur = max(nums[i], cur + nums[i]): *extend* the run or *restart* at i
i = 0: start, cur = *-2*, best = -2
i = 1: restart, cur = *1*, best = 1
i = 2: extend, cur = *-2*
i = 3: restart, cur = *4*, best = 4
i = 4: extend, cur = *3*
i = 5: extend, cur = *5*, best = 5
i = 6: extend, cur = *6*, best = 6
i = 7: extend, cur = *1*
i = 8: extend, cur = *5*
Best = *6* from the run [4,−1,2,1]
A negative prefix never helps, so drop it: *O(n)* time, *O(1)* space

patterns.name: Longest increasing subsequence
patterns.idea: Patience piles: binary search where each number lands; pile count is the LIS length.
patterns.invariant: tails[k] is the smallest tail of any increasing subsequence of length k+1.
patterns.cue: LIS, Russian doll envelopes, number of LIS, longest chain, bitonic.

problems.title: Minimum Number of Removals to Make Mountain Array

steps: tails stays sorted: binary search where each number *lands*
10 is bigger than every tail: *append*, length 1
9 replaces tails[0] = 10: same length, *smaller tail*
2 replaces tails[0] = 9: same length, *smaller tail*
5 is bigger than every tail: *append*, length 2
3 replaces tails[1] = 5: same length, *smaller tail*
7 is bigger than every tail: *append*, length 3
101 is bigger than every tail: *append*, length 4
18 replaces tails[3] = 101: same length, *smaller tail*
Length of tails = *4* (e.g. 2, 3, 7, 101); tails itself is not the subsequence
One binary search per element: *O(n log n)*

patterns.name: Grid path DP
patterns.idea: dp[r][c] from the cell above and the cell to the left.
patterns.invariant: dp[r][c] is the count/min cost of reaching (r,c) using only right/down moves.
patterns.cue: Unique paths I/II, min path sum, triangle, falling path, dungeon game.

problems.title: Count Square Submatrices with All Ones
Paths in Matrix Whose Sum Is Divisible by K

steps: Only *right* and *down* moves: a cell is reached from above or from the left
Bottom-right holds the answer: *7* (1→3→1→1→1)
Each cell looks at two neighbours: *O(m·n)* time, one row of memory if rolled

patterns.name: 0/1 knapsack (subset sum)
patterns.idea: For each item, sweep capacities downward so each item is used once.
patterns.invariant: dp[c] is true iff some subset of the items so far sums to c.
patterns.cue: Partition equal subset sum, target sum, last stone weight II, ones and zeroes.

problems.title: Partition Array Into Two Arrays to Minimize Sum Difference

steps: dp[0] is true; for each item, dp[c] |= dp[c − item] for c from *high to low*
Item 1: newly reachable sums *1*
Item 5: newly reachable sums *6, 5*
Downward sweep matters: dp[10] used dp[5] from *before* item 5, so 5 is not counted twice
Item 11: newly reachable sums *11*
Item 5: newly reachable sums *10*
dp[11] is true: {1, 5, 5} sums to 11, the array *can* be split
One row of size target per item: *O(n · target)*

patterns.name: Unbounded knapsack (coin change)
patterns.idea: Sweep capacities upward so an item can be reused.
patterns.invariant: dp[a] is the best for amount a using any number of each coin.
patterns.cue: Coin change (min), coin change II (ways), perfect squares, combination sum IV.

problems.title: Number of Dice Rolls With Target Sum

steps: Sweep amounts *upward*: dp[a] = 1 + min(dp[a − coin]) over coins that fit
Upward sweep lets a coin repeat: *O(coins · amount)*

patterns.name: Two-sequence DP (LCS / edit distance)
patterns.idea: dp[i][j] compares prefixes; match takes the diagonal, else the best neighbour.
patterns.invariant: dp[i][j] is the answer for s[:i] and t[:j].
patterns.cue: LCS, edit distance, distinct subsequences, delete operation, interleaving.

problems.title: Minimum ASCII Delete Sum for Two Strings

steps: Match → take the diagonal; else 1 + min(delete ↑, insert ←, replace ↖)
Base row and column: turning a prefix into *empty* costs its length
Row 'r': dp[3][1] = diagonal 2 (match 'r')
dp[5][3] = *3*: replace h→r, delete r, delete e
Fill |s|·|t| cells, each in O(1): *O(n·m)*

patterns.name: Wildcard / regex matching DP
patterns.idea: A star either matches nothing (drop it) or eats one more character.
patterns.invariant: dp[i][j] says s[:i] matches p[:j].
patterns.cue: Regular expression matching, wildcard matching.
steps: '?' matches one char; '*' matches *nothing* (look left) or *one more* char (look up)
Row ε: only a prefix of stars matches the empty string
Row 'a': star columns copy ← or ↑; letter columns need a match ↖
Row 'd': star columns copy ← or ↑; letter columns need a match ↖
Row 'c': star columns copy ← or ↑; letter columns need a match ↖
Row 'e': star columns copy ← or ↑; letter columns need a match ↖
Row 'b': star columns copy ← or ↑; letter columns need a match ↖
dp[5][4] is *✓*: '*' ate 'adc', 'e' went to the 2nd '*', 'b' matched
|s| × |p| table, O(1) per cell: *O(n·m)*

patterns.name: Palindromes: expand or table
patterns.idea: Expand around each centre, or dp[i][j] = s[i]==s[j] and dp[i+1][j−1].
patterns.invariant: dp[i][j] is true iff s[i..j] is a palindrome.
patterns.cue: Longest palindromic substring/subsequence, count palindromic substrings, partitioning.

problems.title: Minimum Insertion Steps to Make a String Palindrome

steps: Every palindrome has a *centre*: expand outward while the ends match
Centre 0 ('b'): a single letter is a palindrome
Hit the edge: stop
Centre 1 ('a'): a single letter is a palindrome
s[0] = s[2] = 'b': *expand* to 'bab'
Centre 2 ('b'): a single letter is a palindrome
s[1] = s[3] = 'a': *expand* to 'aba'
Centre 3 ('a'): a single letter is a palindrome
Centre 4 ('d'): a single letter is a palindrome
Hit the edge: stop
Even centres (between letters) found nothing; answer *'bab'* (or 'aba')
2n−1 centres, each expands O(n): *O(n²)*, O(1) space

patterns.name: Prefix segmentation DP
patterns.idea: dp[i] is true if some j < i has dp[j] true and s[j:i] in the dictionary.
patterns.invariant: dp[i] says s[:i] can be fully segmented.
patterns.cue: Word break I/II, concatenated words, decode ways, minimum extra characters.
steps: dp[0] is true; dp[i] is true if some dp[j] is true and s[j:i] is a *word*
i = 2: from dp[0] ✓, s[0:2] = 'le' is not a word → dp[2] stays ·
i = 4: dp[0] ✓ and s[0:4] = 'leet' is a word → dp[4] = *✓*
i = 5: from dp[4] ✓, s[4:5] = 'c' is not a word → dp[5] stays ·
i = 7: from dp[4] ✓, s[4:7] = 'cod' is not a word → dp[7] stays ·
i = 8: dp[4] ✓ and s[4:8] = 'code' is a word → dp[8] = *✓*
dp[8] is ✓: 'leet' + 'code' → *true*
Each i tries every j: *O(n²)* with a word set (O(n·L) with a trie)

patterns.name: Interval DP (last operation)
patterns.idea: Choose the last element burst/removed in [i, j]; the sides become independent.
patterns.invariant: dp[i][j] is the best for the subarray i..j treated alone.
patterns.cue: Burst balloons, minimum cost to merge stones, strange printer, remove boxes, matrix chain.

problems.title: Guess Number Higher or Lower II
Minimum Cost Tree From Leaf Values

steps: Pick the balloon burst *last* in (i, j): its neighbours are then i and j, so the two sides are independent
dp[0][5] = *167*: the whole array, every length filled from short to long
n² intervals × n split points: *O(n³)*

patterns.name: State-machine DP (stocks)
patterns.idea: States: holding / not holding (plus cooldown); transitions carry the best cash.
patterns.invariant: hold = best cash while holding a share; free = best cash with none.
patterns.cue: Stock II/III/IV, with cooldown, with fee.

problems.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock II
Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock with Cooldown
Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock III
Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock IV
Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock with Transaction Fee

steps: Three states: *hold* a share, just *sold* (cooldown), or *rest*
Day 0, price 1: hold = *-1*, sold = *−∞*, rest = *0*
Day 1, price 2: hold = *-1*, sold = *1*, rest = *0*
Day 2, price 3: hold = *-1*, sold = *2*, rest = *1*
Day 3, price 0: hold = *1*, sold = *-1*, rest = *2*
Day 4, price 2: hold = *1*, sold = *3*, rest = *2*
Why rest − p for buying: you can only buy from *rest*, never right after a sale
max(sold, rest) at the end = *3*: buy 1 sell 3 · cool · buy 0 sell 2
One pass, three numbers of state: *O(n)* time, *O(1)* space

patterns.name: Bitmask DP over subsets
patterns.idea: The mask records which items are used; add one item per transition.
patterns.invariant: dp[mask] is the best over exactly the items in mask.
patterns.cue: Shortest path visiting all nodes, partition to k subsets, parallel courses II, minimum XOR sum.

problems.title: Partition to K Equal Sum Subsets
Find Minimum Time to Finish All Jobs

patterns.example: Assign 3 jobs to 3 workers by mask
steps: A mask of workers already used; its popcount says how many jobs are placed
2ⁿ masks, n transitions each: *O(2ⁿ · n)* instead of n! orderings

patterns.name: Memoised DFS (top-down)
patterns.idea: Recurse on the natural subproblem and cache by its parameters.
patterns.invariant: cache[state] is final once filled.
patterns.cue: Longest increasing path in a matrix, target sum, out of boundary paths, knight probability.

problems.title: Longest Increasing Path in a Matrix
Minimum Time to Finish the Race
Number of Ways to Form a Target String Given a Dictionary

steps: Ask each cell: how long is the best path starting from you? *Cache* the answer
Visit (0,0) = 9: try every *bigger* neighbour
memo[0][0] = *1*, cached for good
Visit (1,0) = 6: try every *bigger* neighbour
(0,0) is cached: reuse *1*, no recursion
memo[1][0] = *2*, cached for good
Visit (2,0) = 2: try every *bigger* neighbour
(1,0) is cached: reuse *2*, no recursion
memo[2][0] = *3*, cached for good
Visit (2,1) = 1: try every *bigger* neighbour
Visit (1,1) = 6: try every *bigger* neighbour
Visit (1,2) = 8: try every *bigger* neighbour
memo[1][2] = *1*, cached for good
Visit (0,1) = 9: try every *bigger* neighbour
memo[0][1] = *1*, cached for good
memo[1][1] = *2*, cached for good
memo[2][1] = *4*, cached for good
The remaining cells fill the same way; the answer is the largest entry: *4* (1→2→6→9)
Each cell is solved once and reused: *O(m·n)* instead of exponential

patterns.name: Digit DP
patterns.idea: Build the number digit by digit with a 'tight' flag and the needed state.
patterns.invariant: dp[pos][tight][state] counts completions of the prefix.
patterns.cue: Count numbers with unique digits, numbers at most N given digit set, count good numbers.

problems.title: Numbers At Most N Given Digit Set

steps: *tight* = prefix equals N so far; *free* = already smaller, anything goes
At the end there is exactly *1* way to finish (the empty suffix)
free[2] = 3 choices × free[3] = *3*
free[1] = 3 choices × free[2] = *9*
free[0] = 3 choices × free[1] = *27*
tight[2]: 2 digit(s) below 4 × free[3] + 0 since 4 is not allowed = *2*
tight[1]: 1 digit(s) below 3 × free[2] + tight[2] since 3 is allowed = *5*
tight[0]: 1 digit(s) below 2 × free[1] + 0 since 2 is not allowed = *9*
3-digit numbers ≤ 234: tight[0] = *9*; shorter numbers are free: 3 + 9 = *12*
digits × (tight, free) × choices: *O(len · 10)*, never enumerate 234 numbers

patterns.name: Game DP (minimax on a range)
patterns.idea: Score difference view: best = max over moves of (gain − opponent's best).
patterns.invariant: dp[i][j] is the best score difference the mover can force on piles i..j.
patterns.cue: Predict the winner, stone game I/II/III, can I win, flip game II.
steps: Think in *score difference*: my gain minus whatever the opponent then forces
One pile: the mover takes it, lead = its value
Fill by range length: *pairs* first, then the whole array
dp[0][2] = *-2* < 0: player 1 cannot win on [1,5,2]
Every range once, two moves each: *O(n²)*

patterns.name: Counting ways with modulo
patterns.idea: Sum the ways from every predecessor state, mod 1e9+7.
patterns.invariant: dp[i] counts distinct constructions of the first i positions.
patterns.cue: Decode ways, unique paths, number of music playlists, dice rolls, count vowels permutation.

problems.title: Number of Dice Rolls With Target Sum
Number of Ways to Stay in the Same Place After Some Steps

steps: dp[0] = *1*: the empty prefix decodes one way
dp[2]: '2' alone → dp[1] = 1 + '12' as one letter → dp[0] = 1 = *2*
dp[3]: '2' alone → dp[2] = 2 + '22' as one letter → dp[1] = 1 = *3*
dp[4]: '6' alone → dp[3] = 3 + '26' as one letter → dp[2] = 2 = *5*
Each dp[i] sums two earlier states; *mod* keeps the numbers small
A Fibonacci-shaped recurrence: *O(n)* time, two variables of memory

patterns.name: DP over sorted keys (chains)
patterns.idea: Sort by size; dp[item] extends from the best smaller item it can follow.
patterns.invariant: dp[x] is the longest chain ending at x, and all shorter items are already final.
patterns.cue: Longest string chain, largest divisible subset, longest arithmetic subsequence.

problems.title: Longest Arithmetic Subsequence of Given Difference

patterns.example: Longest String Chain on [a, b, ba, bca, bda, bdca]
steps: Sort by length: every predecessor of a word is already *final* when we reach it
'a': no shorter word by deleting one char, chain = *1*
'b': no shorter word by deleting one char, chain = *1*
'ba' → drop a char → a, b; chain = 1 + best of them = *2*
'bca' → drop a char → ba; chain = 1 + best of them = *3*
'bda' → drop a char → ba; chain = 1 + best of them = *3*
'bdca' → drop a char → bca, bda; chain = 1 + best of them = *4*
Longest chain = *4*: a → ba → bda → bdca
Sort once, then n words × L deletions: *O(n log n + n·L²)*

patterns.name: Furthest reach (jump game)
patterns.idea: Track the furthest index reachable; a new level starts when you pass the current edge.
patterns.invariant: Every index ≤ reach is reachable with the current number of jumps.
patterns.cue: Jump game I/II, video stitching, minimum taps to water a garden.

problems.title: Minimum Number of Taps to Open to Water a Garden

steps: Scan once; *farthest* = furthest index reachable so far, *end* = edge of the current jump
i=0: can reach 0+2 = 2, farthest = *2*
i reached end: take jump *1*, new end = farthest = 2
i=1: can reach 1+3 = 4, farthest = *4*
i=2: can reach 2+1 = 3, farthest = *4*
i reached end: take jump *2*, new end = farthest = 4
i=3: can reach 3+1 = 4, farthest = *4*
Index 4 is inside the current jump: *2* jumps (0→1→4)
One pass, no DP table: *O(n)* time, *O(1)* space

patterns.name: Sort, then take greedily
patterns.idea: Order by the key that an exchange argument proves safe, then commit one by one.
patterns.invariant: No swap of two chosen decisions can improve the result.
patterns.cue: Assign cookies, boats to save people, two city scheduling, minimum cost to hire.

problems.title: Reduce Array Size to The Half

steps: Sort first; pair the *heaviest* person with the *lightest* if they fit
Exchange argument: if the heaviest can share, sharing with the lightest never hurts
3 goes *alone* (too heavy to share)
1 + 2 = 3 ≤ 3: they *share* a boat
2 goes *alone* (last person)
Pointers crossed: *3* boats
Sort *O(n log n)*, then one two-pointer sweep

patterns.name: Reset-on-negative sweep
patterns.idea: Walk once; whenever the running tank goes negative, restart from the next index.
patterns.invariant: If total ≥ 0, the last restart index is a valid start.
patterns.cue: Gas station, max subarray (Kadane cousin), minimum start value.

problems.title: Minimum Value to Get Positive Step by Step Sum

steps: Walk once; *tank* resets when it drops below zero, *total* never resets
i=0: tank = -2 < 0, nothing before 1 can be the start; *restart* at 1
i=1: tank = -2 < 0, nothing before 2 can be the start; *restart* at 2
i=2: tank = -2 < 0, nothing before 3 can be the start; *restart* at 3
i=3: tank +0 +3 = *3*, still ≥ 0
i=4: tank +3 +3 = *6*, still ≥ 0
total = 0 ≥ 0, so a tour exists; the last restart *3* is the answer
One pass, two counters: *O(n)* time, *O(1)* space

patterns.name: Last-occurrence partition
patterns.idea: Extend the current chunk to the last occurrence of every char inside it.
patterns.invariant: A chunk closes exactly when its index reaches the max last-occurrence seen.
patterns.cue: Partition labels, max chunks to make sorted, merge intervals by reach.

problems.title: Max Chunks To Make Sorted II

steps: Precompute each letter's *last* index; a part cannot close before them
'a' last appears at 8: end stretches to *8*
'b' last at 5 ≤ 8: end stays
'a' last at 8 ≤ 8: end stays
'b' last at 5 ≤ 8: end stays
'c' last at 7 ≤ 8: end stays
'b' last at 5 ≤ 8: end stays
'a' last at 8 ≤ 8: end stays
'c' last at 7 ≤ 8: end stays
i = end = 8: close a part of size *9*
'd' last appears at 14: end stretches to *14*
'e' last appears at 15: end stretches to *15*
'f' last at 11 ≤ 15: end stays
'e' last at 15 ≤ 15: end stays
'g' last at 13 ≤ 15: end stays
'd' last at 14 ≤ 15: end stays
i = end = 15: close a part of size *7*
Parts: *9, 7* (not 8 + 8: the 'd' and 'e' would be split)
Two passes over the string: *O(n)* time, 26 counters

patterns.name: Two-pass neighbour constraints
patterns.idea: Left-to-right fixes one side's rule, right-to-left fixes the other; take the max.
patterns.invariant: After both passes every local constraint holds with minimal values.
patterns.cue: Candy, trapping rain water (two arrays), product except self, minimum cost tree.

problems.title: Minimum Number of Increments on Subarrays to Form a Target Array

steps: Start everyone at *1* candy; fix the left rule, then the right rule
left→right: 0 ≤ 1, candy[1] stays *1*
left→right: 2 > 0, so candy[2] = candy[1] + 1 = *2*
left→right: 2 ≤ 2, candy[3] stays *1*
left→right: 1 ≤ 2, candy[4] stays *1*
right→left: 2 > 1: candy[3] = max(own, candy[4] + 1) = *2*
right→left: 2 ≤ 2, candy[2] unchanged
right→left: 0 ≤ 2, candy[1] unchanged
right→left: 1 > 0: candy[0] = max(own, candy[1] + 1) = *2*
Both rules hold everywhere with minimal values: total = *8*
Two linear passes: *O(n)* time, one extra array

patterns.name: Counting-based greedy (small alphabet)
patterns.idea: Count letters/values, then construct the best answer from the counts.
patterns.invariant: The construction only needs the multiset, never the order.
patterns.cue: Longest palindrome, reorganise string, task scheduler math form, string balancing.

problems.title: Split a String in Balanced Strings

steps: Count letters; the answer only depends on the *multiset* of counts
'a' × 1: 0 pair(s) add *0*, one left over
'b' × 1: 0 pair(s) add *0*, one left over
'c' × 4: 2 pair(s) add *4*
'd' × 2: 1 pair(s) add *2*
Any one leftover letter can sit in the *middle*: +1
Longest palindrome = *7*, e.g. dccaccd
One counting pass over a 52-letter alphabet: *O(n)* time, *O(1)* space

patterns.name: Trie for prefix queries
patterns.idea: A tree of characters; a path spells a word, a flag marks word ends.
patterns.invariant: Every stored word is a root-to-flag path.
patterns.cue: Implement trie, add and search with wildcards, autocomplete, replace words.

problems.title: Design Add and Search Words Data Structure

steps: Start with an empty root
insert 'apple': no child 'a', *create* it
insert 'apple': no child 'p', *create* it
insert 'apple': no child 'p', *create* it
insert 'apple': no child 'l', *create* it
insert 'apple': no child 'e', *create* it
End of 'apple': mark node 'e' as a *word end*
insert 'app': a → p → p already exist, just *walk* them
Mark the second 'p' as a word end too: the path is *shared*
insert 'ape': a, p exist; 'e' is a *new branch* under p
search('app'): walk a, p, p and the node has ✓ → *true*
startsWith('ap'): the path exists, no ✓ needed → *true*
search('apl'): after a, p there is no child 'l' → *false*
Every operation walks one character per step: *O(L)*

patterns.name: Trie-guided grid DFS
patterns.idea: Build a trie of all words; walk the grid and the trie together, pruning dead branches.
patterns.invariant: The DFS position in the trie matches the path spelled so far.
patterns.cue: Word search II, stream of characters, concatenated words.
patterns.example: Word Search II for [oath, eat] on a 3×3 board
steps: Put every word in one *trie*; a cell is worth visiting only if the trie has that child
Start at (0,0) 'o': root has child 'o', *enter* it
Neighbour (1,0) 'e': node 'o' has no child 'e' → *prune* that branch
Neighbour (0,1) 'a': child exists, go deeper
(1,1) 'a': no child 'a' → *prune*; (0,2) 't' → go on
(1,2) 'h': child exists and it is a *word end*: found 'oath'
Unmark the path on the way back; the trie branch for 'oath' can be *removed* (no more hits)
Start at (1,0) 'e': root has child 'e'
(1,1) 'a' then (2,1) 't': both match, 't' is a word end: found 'eat'
Other starts ('t', 'i', 'k', …) die at the root: no such child
The trie prunes almost every path: far better than one DFS per word

patterns.name: Binary trie for maximum XOR
patterns.idea: Insert numbers bit by bit; for a query walk the opposite bit whenever possible.
patterns.invariant: The greedy walk maximises the result from the most significant bit down.
patterns.cue: Maximum XOR of two numbers, maximum XOR with an element, count pairs with XOR in range.

problems.title: Maximum XOR of Two Numbers in an Array
Maximum XOR With an Element From Array

steps: Insert every number bit by bit, high bit first
insert 5 = 101
insert 2 = 010
insert 7 = 111
insert 3 = 011
query 5 = 101: at each level take the *opposite* bit if it exists
walk gives partner 010 = 2: 5 ⊕ 2 = *7*
query 2 = 010: at each level take the *opposite* bit if it exists
walk gives partner 101 = 5: 2 ⊕ 5 = *7*
Repeat for every number; the maximum pair XOR is *7* (5 ⊕ 2)
n inserts and n queries of 32 steps each: *O(32·n)*

patterns.name: KMP failure function
patterns.idea: The prefix table lets a mismatch jump without re-scanning the text.
patterns.invariant: lps[i] is the longest proper prefix of p[:i+1] that is also a suffix.
patterns.cue: Find first occurrence, shortest palindrome, repeated substring pattern.

problems.title: Find the Index of the First Occurrence in a String

steps: First a table on the *pattern alone*: how far can a mismatch fall back?
lps[0..2]: 'a' → 0, 'aa' → 1 (prefix a = suffix a), 'aab' → 0
'aaba' → 1, 'aabaa' → 2, 'aabaaa' → 2, 'aabaaab' → 3 ('aab')
Characters match: move *both* pointers forward
All 7 match: pattern found at *0*; fall back to j = lps[6] = 3
'a' = p[3]: match, j = 4
'a' = p[4]: match, j = 5
'a' = p[5]: match, j = 6
'c' ≠ p[6]: *slide* j = lps[5] = 2, i stays
'c' ≠ p[2]: *slide* j = lps[1] = 1, i stays
'c' ≠ p[1]: *slide* j = lps[0] = 0, i stays
'c' ≠ p[0] with nothing to fall back on: advance i
Text pointer never moves backwards: match at *0*, scan done
Table O(m), scan O(n): *O(n + m)* instead of O(n·m)

patterns.name: Rolling hash (Rabin–Karp)
patterns.idea: Hash a window; slide by removing the left char and adding the right.
patterns.invariant: The hash describes exactly the current window.
patterns.cue: Repeated DNA sequences, longest duplicate substring, string matching, distinct substrings.

problems.title: Find the Index of the First Occurrence in a String
Sum of Scores of Built Strings

patterns.example: Rolling hash of length-3 windows over 'abcab'
steps: Window 0 'abc': 1·100 + 2·10 + 3 = *123*, computed in full once
Hash 312 equals the target: *verify* the characters, 'cab' found at 2
A hash match is only a candidate: compare the characters to rule out *collisions*
Each slide is constant work: *O(n)* expected for pattern search or duplicate windows

patterns.name: Reverse-and-build string transforms
patterns.idea: Reverse in chunks, or build the answer backwards with a buffer.
patterns.invariant: Each chunk is independent; the buffer holds one unit at a time.
patterns.cue: Reverse words, reverse words in place, zigzag, string compression, text justification.

problems.title: Reverse Words in a String III

patterns.example: Reverse Words in 'the sky is blue'
steps: Two reversals: whole string first, then each *word* on its own
Reverse the whole string: words are in the right order but *spelled backwards*
Reverse 'eulb' → '*blue*'
Reverse 'si' → '*is*'
Reverse 'yks' → '*sky*'
Reverse 'eht' → '*the*'
Result: 'blue is the sky', built *in place*
Two linear passes, no extra buffer: *O(n)* time, *O(1)* space

patterns.name: Parse with a state machine
patterns.idea: Walk characters once with explicit states: sign, digits, overflow guard.
patterns.invariant: The state fully describes the valid prefix parsed so far.
patterns.cue: atoi, valid number, roman numerals, version compare, fraction to decimal.
steps: Explicit states: skip spaces, read one sign, then digits, then *stop*
SPACE: skip leading blanks
SIGN: '-' sets sign = *−*, allowed only once
DIGITS: value = value·10 + 4 = *4* (overflow check first)
DIGITS: value = value·10 + 2 = *42* (overflow check first)
'a' is not a digit: *END*, everything after is ignored
Apply the sign: *-42*, clamped to the 32-bit range if needed
One pass over the characters: *O(n)*, no regex, no surprises

patterns.name: Merge / compare two strings in lockstep
patterns.idea: Advance pointers through both strings together; handle leftovers.
patterns.invariant: i and j always point at the next unused character of each string.
patterns.cue: Merge strings alternately, is subsequence, longest common prefix, backspace compare.
steps: Two pointers in *lockstep*: j always moves, i moves only on a match
t[0] = 'a' matches s[0]: advance *both*
t[1] = 'h' ≠ s[1]: skip it, advance *j only*
t[2] = 'b' matches s[1]: advance *both*
t[3] = 'g' ≠ s[2]: skip it, advance *j only*
t[4] = 'd' ≠ s[2]: skip it, advance *j only*
t[5] = 'c' matches s[2]: advance *both*
i reached the end of s: every character was found in order → *true*
Each pointer only moves forward: *O(n + m)* time, *O(1)* space

patterns.name: XOR cancels pairs
patterns.idea: a ⊕ a = 0, so pairs vanish and the lone element survives.
patterns.invariant: The running XOR equals the XOR of unpaired elements.
patterns.cue: Single number, missing number, find the difference, single number III.
steps: XOR everything into one accumulator, starting at 0
Bring in 4 = 0100
acc ⊕ x = *4*: a bit stays 1 only where exactly one side has it
Bring in 1 = 0001
acc ⊕ x = *5*: a bit stays 1 only where exactly one side has it
Bring in 2 = 0010
acc ⊕ x = *7*: a bit stays 1 only where exactly one side has it
Bring in 1 = 0001
acc ⊕ x = *6*: a bit stays 1 only where exactly one side has it
Bring in 2 = 0010
acc ⊕ x = *4*: a bit stays 1 only where exactly one side has it
The pairs 1⊕1 and 2⊕2 vanished; what survives is *4*
One pass, one integer of memory: *O(n)* time, *O(1)* space

patterns.name: Bit tricks (n & (n−1), masks)
patterns.idea: n & (n−1) clears the lowest set bit; shifts and masks build numbers without arithmetic.
patterns.invariant: Each trick is an identity on the binary representation.
patterns.cue: Power of two, number of 1 bits, counting bits, reverse bits, sum without +.
patterns.example: Count set bits of 13 with n & (n−1)
steps: 13 = *1101*: three set bits, but we never scan them one by one
n − 1 = 1100: borrows flip the lowest 1 and the zeros under it
n & (n−1) = 1100 = 12: lowest set bit gone, count = *1*
n − 1 = 1011: borrows flip the lowest 1 and the zeros under it
n & (n−1) = 1000 = 8: lowest set bit gone, count = *2*
n − 1 = 0111: borrows flip the lowest 1 and the zeros under it
n & (n−1) = 0000 = 0: lowest set bit gone, count = *3*
n is 0 after *3* steps: 13 has 3 set bits
Same trick: n & (n−1) == 0 means n is a *power of two*; n & −n isolates the lowest bit
Loop runs once per set bit: *O(popcount)*, no division

patterns.name: Enumerate subsets by mask
patterns.idea: Masks 0..2^n−1 encode every subset; bit i means item i is in.
patterns.invariant: Each mask maps to exactly one subset.
patterns.cue: Subsets, maximum product of word lengths, beautiful arrangement, can partition.

problems.title: Partition to K Equal Sum Subsets
Find Minimum Time to Finish All Jobs

steps: Masks 0 … 2ⁿ−1 are *all* the subsets: each bit is one include/exclude choice
mask 011 → *{a,b}*
mask 101 → *{a,c}*
mask 110 → *{b,c}*
mask 111 → *{a,b,c}*
8 masks, 8 distinct subsets, no recursion and no duplicates
*O(2ⁿ · n)* to list them; a mask is also a perfect DP state key

patterns.name: Fast exponentiation
patterns.idea: Square the base and halve the exponent; multiply in when the bit is set.
patterns.invariant: result · base^exp is constant across iterations.
patterns.cue: pow(x, n), count good numbers, modular power, matrix power (fibonacci).

problems.title: Number of Ways to Stay in the Same Place After Some Steps

steps: 10 = *1010*: write the exponent in binary
low bit is 0: result unchanged
square the base → 4, shift the exponent → 5
low bit is 1: result = result · base = *4*
square the base → 16, shift the exponent → 2
low bit is 0: result unchanged
square the base → 256, shift the exponent → 1
low bit is 1: result = result · base = *1024*
square the base → 65536, shift the exponent → 0
exp is 0: result = *1024* = 2¹⁰
One squaring per bit: *O(log n)* multiplications; same loop for modular power and matrix power

patterns.name: GCD and number theory
patterns.idea: Euclid: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a mod b); primes by sieve.
patterns.invariant: The gcd never changes under the Euclid step.
patterns.cue: GCD of strings, count primes, ugly numbers, fraction reduction, water jug.

problems.title: Number of Pairs of Interchangeable Rectangles

steps: Any common divisor of a and b also divides a − q·b, so the *remainder* keeps the gcd
48 = 2·18 + *12*: cut 18 out of 48 as often as possible
Shift: a = 18, b = 12
18 = 1·12 + *6*: cut 12 out of 18 as often as possible
Shift: a = 12, b = 6
12 = 2·6 + *0*: cut 6 out of 12 as often as possible
Shift: a = 6, b = 0
b reached 0: gcd(48, 18) = *6*
Each step at least halves one number: *O(log min(a, b))*

patterns.name: Digit-by-digit arithmetic
patterns.idea: Peel digits with % 10 and / 10; rebuild with ×10, guard overflow.
patterns.invariant: The partial result holds exactly the digits consumed so far.
patterns.cue: Reverse integer, palindrome number, plus one, add digits, sqrt, nth digit.
steps: Peel the *last* digit with % 10, drop it with // 10
x % 10 = *3*: the last digit of 123
rev = 0 + 3 = *3*, x becomes 12
x % 10 = *2*: the last digit of 12
rev = 30 + 2 = *32*, x becomes 1
x % 10 = *1*: the last digit of 1
rev = 320 + 1 = *321*, x becomes 0
x is 0: stop. rev = *321*
Guard overflow before each rev × 10 + digit step
One step per digit: *O(log₁₀ x)* time, O(1) space

patterns.name: Random pick and reservoir sampling
patterns.idea: Prefix sums + binary search for weighted pick; reservoir keeps each item with prob 1/i.
patterns.invariant: After i items, each has probability 1/i (reservoir) or weight/total (weighted).
patterns.cue: Random pick with weight, reservoir sampling on lists, shuffle, random pick index.
steps: Heavier items deserve a *bigger* slice of the random range
Draw r = *7* uniformly from 1..10
mid prefix 4 < 7: range becomes [2,3]
mid prefix 6 < 7: range becomes [3,3]
r = 7 lands on index *3* (weight 4, chance 4/10)
Draw r = *1* uniformly from 1..10
mid prefix 4 ≥ 1: range becomes [0,1]
mid prefix 1 ≥ 1: range becomes [0,0]
r = 1 lands on index *0* (weight 1, chance 1/10)
Draw r = *4* uniformly from 1..10
mid prefix 4 ≥ 4: range becomes [0,1]
mid prefix 1 < 4: range becomes [1,1]
r = 4 lands on index *1* (weight 3, chance 3/10)
Prefix once *O(n)*; each pick is a binary search *O(log n)*

patterns.name: Coordinate geometry with hashing
patterns.idea: Hash points or slopes; count rectangles/lines by pairs.
patterns.invariant: A canonical key (dx/gcd, dy/gcd) identifies a direction exactly.
patterns.cue: Minimum area rectangle, max points on a line, k closest, valid square, boomerangs.
steps: Put every point in a *hash set* of (x, y)
Diagonal (1,1)–(3,3): corners (1,3),(3,1) *exist*, area 4
Diagonal (1,1)–(2,2): a corner is *missing*, skip
Diagonal (2,2)–(3,3): a corner is *missing*, skip
Diagonal (1,3)–(4,1): a corner is *missing*, skip
(3,1) and (4,1) share a row or column: *not a diagonal*
(1,1) and (4,1) share a row or column: *not a diagonal*
Every pair of points was tried as a diagonal: best = *4*
Pairs × O(1) set lookups: *O(n²)* time

patterns.name: Matrix traversal and rotation
patterns.idea: Rotate = transpose then reverse rows; spiral = four shrinking bounds.
patterns.invariant: The bounds (top, bottom, left, right) always enclose the unvisited ring.
patterns.cue: Rotate image, spiral matrix I/II, diagonal traverse, set matrix zeroes.
steps: Keep four bounds; walk the *outer ring*, then shrink
Row 0 left→right, then top becomes 1
Column 3 top→bottom, then right becomes 2
Row 2 right→left, then bottom becomes 1
Column 0 bottom→top, then left becomes 1
Row 1 left→right, then top becomes 2
Bounds crossed: every cell visited *exactly once*
Rotation is the cousin: transpose, then reverse each row
*O(m·n)* time, output only

patterns.name: Staircase search in a sorted matrix
patterns.idea: Start at the top-right: go left if too big, down if too small.
patterns.invariant: The target can only lie below-left of the current cell.
patterns.cue: Search a 2D matrix II, count negatives, kth smallest in a sorted matrix (counting).

problems.title: Kth Smallest Element in a Sorted Matrix
Count Negative Numbers in a Sorted Matrix

steps: Start at the *top-right*: left is smaller, down is bigger
15 > 5: the column below is all bigger, *go left*
Candidates shrink to the blue region; now at 11
11 > 5: the column below is all bigger, *go left*
Candidates shrink to the blue region; now at 7
7 > 5: the column below is all bigger, *go left*
Candidates shrink to the blue region; now at 4
4 < 5: the row to the left is all smaller, *go down*
Candidates shrink to the blue region; now at 5
Each step discards a full row or column: at most m + n moves
*O(m + n)* time, O(1) space

patterns.name: Hash map + array for O(1) random
patterns.idea: Array for random access, map from value to its index; delete by swapping with the last.
patterns.invariant: map[v] is the index of v in the array.
patterns.cue: Insert delete getRandom, with duplicates, random set designs.

problems.title: Insert Delete GetRandom O(1) - Duplicates allowed

steps: Array gives *random index* access; map gives O(1) lookup of an element's slot
insert(1): append at index 0, map[1] = *0*
insert(2): append at index 1, map[2] = *1*
insert(3): append at index 2, map[3] = *2*
remove(2): deleting from the middle would shift everything
So *swap* 2 with the last element 3: map[3] = 1
Pop the tail and drop 2 from the map: still O(1)
getRandom(): random index in [0, size) → say index 1 = *3*
insert, remove, getRandom all *O(1)* average

patterns.name: Time-versioned map
patterns.idea: Store (timestamp, value) lists per key; binary search the latest ≤ t.
patterns.invariant: Each key's list is sorted by timestamp.
patterns.cue: Time based key-value store, snapshot array, stock price with timestamps.
patterns.example: TimeMap set foo@1=bar, set foo@4=bar2, get foo@3
steps: Each key owns a list of (timestamp, value), *sorted by timestamp*
set(foo, bar, 1): append to the end
set(foo, bar2, 4): append to the end
set(foo, bar3, 7): append to the end
get(foo, 3): binary search the *last* timestamp ≤ 3
timestamp 1 ≤ 3: answer *bar*
get(foo, 7): binary search the *last* timestamp ≤ 7
timestamp 7 ≤ 7: answer *bar3*
get(foo, 5): binary search the *last* timestamp ≤ 5
timestamp 4 ≤ 5: answer *bar2*
set is O(1) append; get is *O(log n)* per key

patterns.name: Lazy iterators
patterns.idea: Keep a stack/pointer so next() does O(1) work on average.
patterns.invariant: The iterator position always describes the next unreturned element.
patterns.cue: Flatten nested list, BST iterator, peeking iterator, zigzag iterator, compressed string iterator.
steps: Push the list *reversed* so the first element is on top
hasNext(): top is a list, *unpack* it onto the stack
next() → *1*
next() → *1*
next() → *2*
hasNext(): top is a list, *unpack* it onto the stack
next() → *1*
next() → *1*
Stack empty: hasNext() is false
Each element is pushed and popped once: *amortised O(1)* per next()

patterns.name: Ordered intervals (range module)
patterns.idea: Keep disjoint sorted intervals; add merges neighbours, remove splits them.
patterns.invariant: The stored intervals are disjoint and sorted at all times.
patterns.cue: Range module, my calendar I/II/III, data stream disjoint intervals, exam room.
steps: Keep a *sorted list of disjoint* half-open ranges
add [10,20): nothing overlaps, insert it
remove [14,16): find ranges overlapping it
Cut: keep the left piece [10,14) and the right piece *[16,20)*
query [13,15): find the range starting at or before 13
[10,14) ends at 14 < 15: *not fully covered* → false
add [16,18): it overlaps [16,20)
Merge overlapping neighbours into one range: still [16,20)
query [16,19): inside [16,20) → *true*
Binary search for the neighbours: *O(log n)* per op

patterns.name: Segment tree (range query + point update)
patterns.idea: A binary tree of ranges; a query visits O(log n) nodes, an update climbs one path.
patterns.invariant: Each node holds the aggregate of its whole range.
patterns.cue: Range sum query mutable, count of smaller after self, falling squares, my calendar III.

problems.title: Count of Smaller Numbers After Self

patterns.example: Range sum on [1,3,5,7,9,11], update index 1, query [1,3]
steps: Each node stores the *sum of its whole range*; the root covers [0,5]
query [1,3]: descend; a node fully inside is taken whole
Taken nodes 3 + 5 + 7 = *15*
update index 1 → 10: change the leaf
Query touches O(log n) nodes; update climbs one path: *O(log n)* each

patterns.name: Fenwick tree (binary indexed tree)
patterns.idea: Prefix sums in O(log n) by walking the lowest set bit up and down.
patterns.invariant: tree[i] covers the range (i − lowbit(i), i].
patterns.cue: Count of smaller numbers after self, reverse pairs, create sorted array, range sum mutable.

problems.title: Count of Smaller Numbers After Self

steps: Each tree slot sums a block whose length is its *lowest set bit*
tree[1] = sum of array[0..0] = *1* (lowbit 1)
tree[2] = sum of array[0..1] = *4* (lowbit 2)
tree[3] = sum of array[2..2] = *5* (lowbit 1)
tree[4] = sum of array[0..3] = *16* (lowbit 4)
tree[5] = sum of array[4..4] = *9* (lowbit 1)
tree[6] = sum of array[4..5] = *20* (lowbit 2)
prefix(5): start at i = 5, walk down by *clearing the lowest bit*
add tree[5] = 9 → sum 9; i = 5 − 1 = 4
add tree[4] = 16 → sum 25; i = 4 − 4 = 0
prefix(5) = *25* from only 2 slots
update array[3] += 2: climb i = 4, then i += lowbit(i)
Both walks touch one slot per bit: *O(log n)* query and update

patterns.name: Ordered set / sorted container
patterns.idea: Keep a sorted multiset; bisect for neighbours, insert/delete in O(log n).
patterns.invariant: The container is always sorted, so neighbours are adjacent.
patterns.cue: Contains duplicate III, sliding window median, 132 pattern, exam room, my calendar.

problems.title: Count of Smaller Numbers After Self
Kth Largest Element in a Stream
Longest Continuous Subarray With Absolute Diff Less Than or Equal to Limit

patterns.example: Contains Duplicate III window k=3, t=0 on [1,5,9,1,5,9]
steps: Keep the window's values in a *sorted container*; neighbours of x are one bisect away
x = 1: nearest values — / —, none within 0
insert 1 in sorted position
x = 5: nearest values 1 / —, none within 0
insert 5 in sorted position
x = 9: nearest values 5 / —, none within 0
insert 9 in sorted position
x = 1: neighbour 1 is within t = 0 → *true*
Insert, remove and neighbour lookup are all *O(log k)*: O(n log k) total

patterns.name: Bucketing by value range
patterns.idea: Bucket id = value // (t+1); near values land in the same or neighbouring bucket.
patterns.invariant: Two values within t are at most one bucket apart.
patterns.cue: Contains duplicate III, maximum gap, k-diff pairs.
steps: n numbers in range [1,20]: some gap is at least ⌈19/5⌉ = *4*, the bucket width
3 → bucket 0: update its min/max
6 → bucket 1: update its min/max
9 → bucket 2: update its min/max
1 → bucket 0: update its min/max
14 → bucket 3: update its min/max
20 → bucket 4: update its min/max
Gaps *inside* a bucket are < width, so only gaps *between* buckets matter
gap = min of bucket 1 − max of bucket 0 = 6 − 3 = *3*
gap = min of bucket 2 − max of bucket 1 = 9 − 6 = *3*
gap = min of bucket 3 − max of bucket 2 = 14 − 9 = *5*
gap = min of bucket 4 − max of bucket 3 = 20 − 14 = *6*
Maximum gap = *6* (between 9 and 14)
Linear buckets instead of sorting: *O(n)* time and space

patterns.name: Matrix exponentiation for recurrences
patterns.idea: A linear recurrence is a matrix; raise it to the nth power by squaring.
patterns.invariant: M^n applied to the base vector gives the nth term.
patterns.cue: Fibonacci in O(log n), climbing stairs, counting strings of length n.

problems.title: Number of Ways to Stay in the Same Place After Some Steps

steps: Fibonacci is a *linear recurrence*, so n steps = one matrix power
Write 10 in binary: *1010*; square the base, multiply in where a bit is 1
bit is 0: result unchanged
square the base → [[2, 1], [1, 1]]; exp becomes 5
bit is 1: result = result × base = [[2, 1], [1, 1]]
square the base → [[5, 3], [3, 2]]; exp becomes 2
bit is 0: result unchanged
square the base → [[34, 21], [21, 13]]; exp becomes 1
bit is 1: result = result × base = [[89, 55], [55, 34]]
Only ⌈log₂ n⌉ squarings: *O(k³ log n)* for a k×k matrix

patterns.name: Candidate elimination (Guess the Word)
patterns.idea: Guess the word that would split candidates most evenly; keep only consistent ones.
patterns.invariant: Every remaining candidate matches all past answers.
patterns.cue: Guess the word, find in mountain array, search unknown-size array, master-mind style.

problems.title: Guess Number Higher or Lower II
Search in a Sorted Array of Unknown Size
Minimum Path Cost in a Hidden Grid

steps: Every surviving candidate must agree with *all* past answers
Score each candidate by how evenly it splits the others by match count
Guess *abcczz*: smallest worst-case bucket (2)
The judge answers *2* matching positions
Keep only words with exactly 2 matches vs abcczz: *2* left
Guess *ccbazz*: smallest worst-case bucket (1)
The judge answers *2* matching positions
Keep only words with exactly 2 matches vs ccbazz: *1* left
Guess *eiowzz*: smallest worst-case bucket (1)
The judge answers *6* matching positions
6 of 6: *found* the secret in 3 guesses
Each guess costs O(n²·L) to choose; candidates shrink fast

patterns.name: Careful state simulation
patterns.idea: Model the rules exactly; keep the state minimal and update it in order.
patterns.invariant: The modelled state is enough to decide the next step.
patterns.cue: Game of life, spiral, robot bounded, text justification, time to cross the door.

problems.title: Time Taken to Cross the Door

patterns.example: Game of Life one generation on a 4×3 board
steps: Every cell looks at its *8 neighbours* in the old board, never the new one
(1,1) is alive with 3 live neighbours: *stays alive*
(0,0) is dead with 3 live neighbours: *is born*
(1,3) is alive with 0 live neighbours: *dies*
(0,1) is alive with 2 live neighbours: *stays alive*
(2,1) is alive with 2 live neighbours: *stays alive*
(1,0) is alive with 3 live neighbours: *stays alive*
The remaining cells follow the same rule
Only now does the new board *replace* the old one
In-place trick: encode old+new in one cell (e.g. 2 = was alive, now dead)
*O(m·n)* per generation; model the rules exactly, update in order

patterns.name: Meet in the middle
patterns.idea: Split into two halves, enumerate each, match complements with a sorted list or set.
patterns.invariant: Every full subset is one left subset plus one right subset.
patterns.cue: Partition to minimise sum difference, closest subsequence sum, 4Sum II.

problems.title: Partition Array Into Two Arrays to Minimize Sum Difference
Ways to Split Array Into Three Subarrays

steps: 2^n subsets is too many; 2·2^(n/2) is fine. *Split* the array
Left half [5, -7]: subset sums [0, 5, -7, -2]
Right half [3, 5]: subset sums *sorted* [0, 3, 5, 8]
left 0: need 6; nearest right sum 5 → |5 − 6| = *1*
left 5: need 1; nearest right sum 0 → |5 − 6| = *1*
left -7: need 13; nearest right sum 8 → |1 − 6| = *5*
left -2: need 8; nearest right sum 8 → |6 − 6| = *0*
Closest subsequence sum differs from the goal by *0*
Enumerate 2^(n/2) per side, binary search to match: *O(2^(n/2) · n)*

patterns.name: Streaming data structures
patterns.idea: Process one item at a time with O(1) or O(log n) state; never store the whole stream.
patterns.invariant: The state summarises the stream so far exactly enough for the queries.
patterns.cue: Moving average, kth largest in a stream, first unique in a stream, median.

problems.title: Kth Largest Element in a Stream
Product of the Last K Numbers

patterns.example: First Unique Number stream: 2,3,5 ; add 5 ; add 2
steps: Never store the whole stream: a *queue* of candidates plus a *count* map
add(2): count becomes 1, push to the queue
add(3): count becomes 1, push to the queue
add(5): count becomes 1, push to the queue
showFirstUnique() → *2*
add(5): count 2, *no longer unique*; lazily stays queued
add(2): count 2, *no longer unique*; lazily stays queued
add(1): new value, push it
front 2 has count 2 > 1: *stale*, pop it
showFirstUnique() → *3*
Each value is pushed once and popped once: *amortised O(1)* per call

patterns.name: Multi-pattern scan with a set of lengths
patterns.idea: For each position try every dictionary length; a hash set makes each check O(L).
patterns.invariant: Each candidate substring is checked exactly once per length.
patterns.cue: Replace words, find and replace in string, apply substitutions, word break check.
patterns.example: Find And Replace in String on 'abcd' with (0,'a','eee'),(2,'cd','ffff')
steps: Index the rules by position: *{0: a→eee, 2: cd→ffff, 5: xy→zz}*
i = 0: s[0:1] = 'a' matches → write *'eee'*
skip ahead by len('a') = 1
i = 1: no rule here, copy 'b'
i = 2: s[2:4] = 'cd' matches → write *'ffff'*
skip ahead by len('cd') = 2
i = 4: no rule here, copy 'c'
i = 5: s[5:7] = 'de' ≠ 'xy' → *no replacement*, copy 'd'
i = 6: no rule here, copy 'e'
i = 7: no rule here, copy 'f'
Result: *eeebffffcdef*
One pass; each rule is tested once against the original: *O(n + Σ|src|)*

patterns.name: Serialize / deserialize by BFS
patterns.idea: Write nodes level by level with null markers; rebuild with a queue of parents.
patterns.invariant: The i-th non-null token is the parent of tokens 2i+1 and 2i+2 in the BFS order.
patterns.cue: Serialize and deserialize binary tree, N-ary tree, tree codec with nulls.
steps: Serialize: BFS, writing *# for a missing child* so the shape survives
pop 1: write 1, enqueue both children (2, 3)
pop 2: write 2, enqueue both children (#, #)
pop 3: write 3, enqueue both children (4, 5)
pop a null: write *#* (it has no children to enqueue)
pop a null: write *#* (it has no children to enqueue)
pop 4: write 4, enqueue both children (#, #)
pop 5: write 5, enqueue both children (#, #)
Serialized: *1 2 3 # # 4 5* (trailing nulls can be dropped)
Deserialize: each parent takes the *next two* tokens as children
Token 0 is the root; put it in the queue
parent 1 takes tokens 1 and 2: 2 and 3
parent 2 takes tokens 3 and 4: # and #
parent 3 takes tokens 5 and 6: 4 and 5
The tree is rebuilt exactly, nulls and all
Both directions visit each node once: *O(n)*

patterns.name: Two-pointer assignment after sorting
patterns.idea: Sort both sides; match the smallest demand with the smallest supply that fits.
patterns.invariant: Each supply is used by the smallest demand it can satisfy.
patterns.cue: Assign cookies, boats, advantage shuffle, max matching of pairs.

problems.title: Maximum Matching of Players With Trainers

steps: Sort both; give the *smallest cookie that fits* to the least greedy child
cookie 1 ≥ greed 1: *assign*, advance both
now child 1 (greed 2) vs cookie 1 (size 1)
cookie 1 < greed 2: too small for anyone left, *skip* the cookie
now child 1 (greed 2) vs cookie 2 (size 3)
cookie 3 ≥ greed 2: *assign*, advance both
now child 2 (greed 3) vs cookie 3 (size 4)
cookie 4 ≥ greed 3: *assign*, advance both
Out of cookies: *3* content children (child with greed 7 gets none)
Exchange argument: a bigger cookie never helps a smaller child more
Sort *O(n log n)*, then one linear two-pointer pass
